sentences.zh: 劉隗，字大連，彭城人，楚元王交之後也。

translations.literal: Liu Kui, courtesy name Dalian, was a native of Pengcheng and a descendant of Prince Yuan of Chu, Liu Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui, whose courtesy name was Dalian, came from Pengcheng and traced his line to Prince Yuan of Chu, Liu Jiao.

sentences.zh: 父砥，東光令。

translations.literal: His father was Liu Di, magistrate of Dongguang.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Liu Di, had served as magistrate of Dongguang.

sentences.zh: 隗少有文翰，起家秘書郎，稍遷冠軍將軍、彭城內史。

translations.literal: Kui in his youth had skill in letters; he began office as a secretary gentleman and was gradually promoted to general who champions the army and interior secretary of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: From an early age Liu Kui showed literary talent; his first appointment was secretary gentleman, and he rose step by step to general who champions the army and interior secretary of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 避亂渡江，元帝以為從事中郎。

translations.literal: Fleeing turmoil he crossed the Yangzi, and Emperor Yuan appointed him attendant gentleman for miscellaneous purposes.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi to escape the chaos, and Emperor Yuan of Jin named him attendant gentleman in the princely staff.

sentences.zh: 隗雅習文史，善求人主意，帝深器遇之。

translations.literal: Kui was well versed in documents and histories and skilled at discerning the ruler's intentions; the emperor greatly esteemed and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui was thoroughly at home in precedent and history and had a knack for reading the emperor's mind; Yuan valued him highly and showered him with favor.

sentences.zh: 遷丞相司直，委以刑憲。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be rectifier for the minister of state and was entrusted with penal law.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to rectifier under the chief minister and given charge of criminal justice.

sentences.zh: 時建康尉收護軍士，而為府將篡取之，隗奏免護軍將軍戴若思官。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiankang commandant seized soldiers of the guards army, but a general of the princely household snatched them away by force; Kui memorialized to dismiss General of the Guards Army Dai Ruosi from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiankang commandant took custody of troops from the guards army only to have a household general wrest them away, Liu Kui impeached the case and secured the removal of Dai Ruosi from the post of general of the guards army.

sentences.zh: 世子文學王籍之居叔母喪而婚，隗奏之，帝下令曰：「《詩》稱殺禮多婚，以會男女之無夫家，正今日之謂也，可一解禁止。

translations.literal: Crown prince's tutor Wang Jizhi, while observing mourning for his aunt by marriage, married; Kui impeached him. The emperor issued an order saying: "The Odes speak of curtailing ritual and many marriages, to bring together men and women who lack spouses; that is exactly what is meant today; it may be uniformly relaxed and forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jizhi, literary attendant to the heir apparent, married while still in mourning for his aunt by marriage; Liu Kui reported him. The emperor replied with an edict: "The Book of Odes allows easing ritual so that more weddings may occur, joining those without families—that is precisely our situation now; let the prohibition be lifted in this one instance."

sentences.zh: 自今以後，宜為其防。

translations.literal: From now on, it is fitting to set safeguards for it.
translations.idiomatic: From this point forward, however, clear rules should keep such abuses in check.

sentences.zh: 」東閣祭酒顏含在叔父喪嫁女，隗又奏之。

translations.literal: " Eastern pavilion libationer Yan Han married off a daughter during mourning for his paternal uncle; Kui again impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan Han, libationer of the Eastern Pavilion, gave his daughter in marriage while mourning his uncle; Liu Kui impeached him as well.

sentences.zh: 廬江太守梁龕明日當除婦服，今日請客奏伎，丞相長史周顗等三十餘人同會，隗奏曰：「夫嫡妻長子皆杖居廬，故周景王有三年之喪，既除而宴，《春秋》猶譏，況龕匹夫，暮宴朝祥，慢服之愆，宜肅喪紀之禮。

translations.literal: Liang Kan, administrator of Lujiang, on the next day was due to lay aside mourning garb for his principal wife; that day he invited guests and had performers play music; chief minister chief clerk Zhou Yi and more than thirty others attended the gathering together. Kui memorialized, saying: "Principal wife and eldest son both staff the mourning hut; therefore King Jing of Zhou, though he had the three-year mourning, when he had laid it aside and held a banquet, the Spring and Autumn still ridiculed him; how much more Kan, a common fellow—feasting at dusk and performing the xiang rite at morning—fault of slighting the garments of mourning; it is fitting to enforce strictly the rites of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Kan, governor of Lujiang, was to end mourning for his wife the following day, yet that very day he threw a banquet with musicians; Zhou Yi, senior clerk to the chief minister, and more than thirty others joined him. Liu Kui submitted a memorial: "A man's wife and eldest son observe the full mourning in the hut; even King Jing of Zhou was faulted in the Spring and Autumn Annals for feasting once the three years were over. Liang Kan is only a private gentleman—carousing at night and holding the 'auspice' rite next morning is a brazen breach of mourning; the code for funerals must be upheld.

sentences.zh: 請免龕官，削侯爵。

translations.literal: I request to dismiss Kan from office and strip marquis rank.
translations.idiomatic: He should be dismissed from office and stripped of his marquisate.

sentences.zh: 顗等知龕有喪，吉會非禮，宜各奪俸一月，以肅其違。

translations.literal: Yi and the others knew Kan was in mourning; auspicious gathering is contrary to ritual; it is fitting each be deprived of salary one month, to enforce their violation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi and the rest knew Liang Kan was in mourning; a festive gathering was improper—they should each forfeit one month's salary as a rebuke for breaking ritual.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 丞相行參軍宋挺，本揚州刺史劉陶門人，陶亡後，挺娶陶愛妾以為小妻。

translations.literal: Acting military adviser to the chief minister Song Ting was originally a disciple of Liu Tao, inspector of Yangzhou; after Tao died, Ting took Tao's beloved concubine as a minor wife.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ting, acting adviser on the chief minister's staff, had once been a follower of Liu Tao, the Yangzhou inspector; after Liu Tao's death he took his patron's favorite concubine as a secondary wife.

sentences.zh: 建興中，挺又割盜官布六百餘匹，正刑棄市，遇赦免。

translations.literal: In the Jianxing era, Ting again embezzled more than six hundred bolts of government cloth; he was sentenced to execution and exposure in the market, but encountered an amnesty and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianxing he was also caught stealing over six hundred bolts of official cloth; he was condemned to public execution but was pardoned in a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 既而奮武將軍阮抗請為長史。

translations.literal: Thereupon general who displays might Ruan Kang requested him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Ruan Kang, general who displays might, asked to appoint him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 隗劾奏曰：「挺蔑其死主而專其室，悖在三之義，傷人倫之序，當投之四裔以禦魑魅。

translations.literal: Kui impeached and memorialized, saying: "Ting despises his dead lord and monopolizes his chamber; he violates the righteousness of the three relationships and injures the order of human ethics; he ought to be cast to the four peripheries to ward off evil spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui impeached him: "Song Ting scorns his dead patron and seizes his household; that tramples the bonds that define the three key relationships and tears at the fabric of society. He should be banished to the frontier to keep demons at bay.

sentences.zh: 請除挺名，禁錮終身。

translations.literal: I request to remove Ting's name and imprison him under lifelong disqualification from office.
translations.idiomatic: Strike his name from the rolls and bar him from office for life.

sentences.zh: 而奮武將軍、太山太守阮抗請為長史。

translations.literal: But general who displays might and Taishan administrator Ruan Kang requested him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ruan Kang, general who displays might and governor of Taishan, was the one who sought Song Ting as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 抗緯文經武，剖符東籓，當庸勳忠良，昵近仁賢，而褒求贓汙，舉頑用嚚。

translations.literal: Kang weaves civil and military, has split tally in the eastern screen; he ought to employ meritorious loyal good men, be intimate with benevolent worthies, yet he praises and seeks filthy corruption, raises the obstinate and employs the vicious.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Kang holds civil and military authority and commands an eastern principality; he should surround himself with loyal, capable men, yet he celebrates the corrupt, elevates the worthless, and appoints the depraved.

sentences.zh: 請免抗官，下獄理罪。

translations.literal: I request to dismiss Kang from office and send him down to prison to settle guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Strip Ruan Kang of his posts and remand him to prison to answer for these charges.

sentences.zh: 」奏可，而挺病死。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved, but Ting died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial, but Song Ting died of illness before sentence could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 隗又奏：「符旨：挺已喪亡，不復追貶。

translations.literal: Kui again memorialized: "According to the directive: Ting has already died; there is no further pursuit of demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui submitted another memorial: "Your written order said that because Song Ting is already dead, no further penalties would be pursued.

sentences.zh: 愚蠢意暗，未達斯義。

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and dim, and has not grasped this meaning.
translations.idiomatic: I am slow-witted and have failed to grasp the full intent of that ruling.

sentences.zh: 昔鄭人ＪＸ子家之棺，漢明追討史遷，經傳褒貶，皆追書先世數百年間，非徒區區欲厘當時，亦將作法垂于來世，當朝亡夕沒便無善惡也。

translations.literal: Formerly the people of Zheng hewed open Zijia's coffin; Han Ming pursued investigation of Sima Qian; in classics and commentaries praise and blame all pursue writing ancestors across several hundred years; it is not merely petty desire to rectify the present, but also will establish models to hang for later generations—if the court dies at dawn and at evening is gone then there is no good and evil.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the people of Zheng broke open Gongsun Zijia's coffin to punish past wrongdoing; Emperor Ming of Han still called Sima Qian to account. The classics and their commentaries judge the dead across centuries—not merely to tidy up the present but to set a precedent for posterity. If someone dies this morning and by evening we may no longer speak of his guilt, moral judgment would mean nothing.

sentences.zh: 請曹如前追除挺名為民，錄妾還本，顯證惡人，班下遠近。

translations.literal: I request the bureau as before pursue removing Ting's name to commoner status, register the concubine and return her to her origin, make evident proof of the wicked man, promulgate to far and near.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the office still strike Song Ting from the registers and reduce him to commoner status, return his concubine to her family, publish the evidence of his crimes, and circulate the judgment throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 南中郎將王含以族強顯貴，驕傲自恣，一請參佐及守長二十許人，多取非其才。

translations.literal: General of the household gentlemen of the south Wang Han, relying on clan strength and eminent nobility, was arrogant and self-indulgent; in one request for aides and defending chiefs about twenty persons, mostly took those not of their talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han, general of household gentlemen in the south, traded on his powerful lineage; arrogant and willful, he once asked for some twenty staff members and county heads, most of them unqualified for their posts.

sentences.zh: 隗劾奏文致甚苦，事雖被寢，王氏深忌疾之。

translations.literal: Kui impeached and memorialized with wording brought to extreme severity; though the affair was tabled, the Wang clan deeply hated and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui framed his impeachment in the harshest terms; although the matter was shelved, the Wang family nursed a deep grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 而隗之彈奏不畏強禦，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Yet as for Kui's impeachments, he did not fear the powerful; all were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui's memorials showed no fear of great houses; time and again he acted in this uncompromising way.

sentences.zh: 建興中，丞相府斬督運令史淳于伯而血逆流，隗又奏曰：「古之為獄必察五聽，三槐九棘以求民情。

translations.literal: In the Jianxing era, the chief minister's office executed transport supervisor clerk Chunyu Bo and blood flowed upward against the current; Kui again memorialized, saying: "In ancient times in conducting prisons one must examine the five hearings, the three huai and nine ji to seek the feelings of the people.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianxing the chief minister's headquarters executed Chunyu Bo, a clerk who oversaw convoys, and his blood ran upward along the pillar; Liu Kui submitted another memorial: "The ancients judged cases only after the fivefold hearing and deliberation under the court's great trees—justice rested on what the people actually knew.

sentences.zh: 雖明庶政，不敢折獄。

translations.literal: Though one clarifies the myriad policies, one dares not decide lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler may master every branch of government, yet still refuse to settle criminal cases alone.

sentences.zh: 死者不得復生，刑者不可復續，是以明王哀矜用刑。

translations.literal: The dead cannot live again; the mutilated cannot be rejoined; therefore enlightened kings pity and are cautious in applying punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The dead cannot be brought back, nor severed limbs restored; that is why wise sovereigns punish only with grief and the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 曹參去齊，以市獄為寄。

translations.literal: When Cao Shen left Qi, he entrusted market and prison to others.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shen left Qi he famously told his successor to leave the market and the jail alone—governance needed a light touch.

sentences.zh: 自頃蒸荒，殺戮無度，罪同斷異，刑罰失宜。

translations.literal: Since recently in steaming waste, killing has been without measure, crimes the same but judgments different, punishments and penalties lose propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, amid turmoil, executions have known no restraint: identical offenses draw different verdicts, and sentencing has lost all proportion.

sentences.zh: 謹按行督運令史淳于伯刑血著柱，遂逆上終極柱末二丈三尺，旋復下流四尺五寸。

translations.literal: Respectfully investigating: when transport supervisor clerk Chunyu Bo was punished, blood adhered to the pillar, then reversed upward to the extreme end of the pillar two zhang three chi, then again flowed down four chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: I have reviewed the file: when Chunyu Bo was executed, his blood clung to the execution post, climbed more than twenty feet against gravity, then ran back down nearly five feet—an omen the crowd could not ignore.

sentences.zh: 百姓喧華，士女縱觀，咸曰其冤。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames clamored; gentlemen and women looked on freely; all said it was his wrongful injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners raised an uproar; men and women lined the streets to watch, and all agreed he had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 伯息忠訴辭稱枉，雲伯督運訖去二月，事畢代還，無有稽乏。

translations.literal: Bo's son Zhong in appeal called it wrongful, saying Bo supervised transport until departure two months; the affair finished and he was replaced and returned; there was no delay or shortage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong petitioned for redress, insisting that Chunyu Bo had finished the convoy duty and handed off two months earlier—his work was complete, his relief had arrived, and he had caused no delay or shortfall.

sentences.zh: 受賕使役，罪不及死。

translations.literal: Receiving bribes and employing labor service, the crime does not reach death.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he took bribes or misused corvée labor, those faults did not merit execution.

sentences.zh: 軍是戍軍，非為征軍，以乏軍興論，於理為枉。

translations.literal: The army is garrison army, not campaign army; to judge by shortage for raising the army is in principle wrongful.
translations.idiomatic: These were garrison troops, not a field army; to condemn him under the statute for wartime supply failures was legally indefensible.

sentences.zh: 四年之中，供給運漕，凡諸徵發租調百役，皆有稽停，而不以軍興論，至於伯也，何獨明之？

translations.literal: Within four years, supplying transport and grain transport, all manner of levies, rent, labor, hundred corvées, all have had delays and stops, yet are not judged by raising the army; as for Bo, why alone make it clear?
translations.idiomatic: For four years every kind of levy—grain, taxes, labor—has run late without anyone invoking the 'wartime emergency' law; why was Chunyu Bo singled out for that harsh standard?

sentences.zh: 捶楚之下，無求不得，囚人畏痛，飾辭應之。

translations.literal: Under flogging, nothing sought is not obtained; prisoners fear pain and embellish words in response.
translations.idiomatic: Under the rod a man will confess to anything; prisoners dread the pain and will say whatever fits the torturer's script.

sentences.zh: 理曹，國之典刑，而使忠等稱冤明時。

translations.literal: The judgment bureau is the state's model punishments, yet it causes Zhong and others to call out wrong in a clear age.
translations.idiomatic: The penal bureau embodies the state's justice; it shames us that Zhong and others must cry injustice in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 謹按從事中郎周筵、法曹參軍劉胤、屬李匡幸荷殊寵，並登列曹，當思敦奉政道，詳法慎殺，使兆庶無枉，人不稱訴。

translations.literal: Respectfully investigating: attendant gentleman Zhou Yan, law bureau military adviser Liu Yin, subordinate Li Kuang have fortunately borne extraordinary favor, all ascended to the bureaus; they ought to think to earnestly uphold the way of governance, examine law and be cautious in killing, so that the myriad common people have no wrong, and people do not call out in complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Zhou Yan, Liu Yin of the law section, and clerk Li Kuang: favored with high office, they should exemplify sound government—study each case, kill only with care, and keep the people from wrongful conviction or public outcry.

sentences.zh: 而令伯枉同周青，冤魂哭於幽都，訴靈恨於黃泉，嗟歎甚于杞梁，血妖過於崩城，故有隕霜之人，夜哭之鬼。

translations.literal: Yet they caused Bo's wrong to match Zhou Qing; wronged souls weep in the dark capital, appeal spirits' hatred in the yellow springs; sighing exceeds Qi Liang, blood prodigy exceeds city-collapse; therefore there are people of falling frost, ghosts weeping at night.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they produced another miscarriage like the case of Zhou Qing: an innocent ghost wails in the underworld, a spirit carries grievance beyond the grave—more pitiable than Qi Liang's widow, more ominous than the blood that toppled a city—until frost falls out of season and phantoms keen in the dark.

sentences.zh: 伯有晝見，彭生為豕，刑殺失中，妖眚並見，以古況今，其揆一也。

translations.literal: Bo You appeared in daylight; Peng Sheng became a pig; punishments and killings missed the mean; prodigies and calamities both appeared; using antiquity to compare to today, its measure is one.
translations.idiomatic: Bo You walked by day, Peng Sheng returned as a swine—when executions misfire, omens multiply. History shows the same pattern we see now.

sentences.zh: 皆由筵等不勝其任，請皆免官。

translations.literal: All are because Yan and the others did not bear their duties; I request all be dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yan and his colleagues failed their charge; I ask that every one of them be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 」於是右將軍王導等上疏引咎，請解職。

translations.literal: " Thereupon General of the Right Wang Dao and others submitted memorials taking blame and requesting to resign office.
translations.idiomatic: On this General of the Right Wang Dao and others offered to resign, accepting responsibility for the affair.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「政刑失中，皆吾暗塞所由。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Government and punishments miss the mean; all are from my darkness and blockage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "When policy and punishment go awry, the fault lies in my own blindness and obstruction.

sentences.zh: 尋示愧懼，思聞忠告，以補其闕。

translations.literal: Soon I showed shame and fear, wished to hear loyal admonition, to repair its gaps.
translations.idiomatic: I am ashamed and alarmed, and I want candid advice to remedy what is lacking.

sentences.zh: 而引過求退，豈所望也！

translations.literal: Yet drawing fault and seeking withdrawal—is that what is hoped for!
translations.idiomatic: But if you all rush to quit, that is hardly what I expect of you!

sentences.zh: 」由是導等一無所問。

translations.literal: " From this Dao and the others were not questioned on anything.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Dao and his colleagues were left in place without reprimand.

sentences.zh: 晉國既建，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: When the Jin state was established, he was appointed vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jin princedom was founded, Liu Kui was named vice censor-in-chief of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 周嵩嫁女，門生斷道解廬，斫傷二人，建康左尉赴變，又被斫。

translations.literal: When Zhou Song married off a daughter, disciples blocked the road and dismantled the hut, hacked and wounded two persons; Jiankang left commandant went to the incident and was again hacked.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhou Song's daughter's wedding his students tore down a roadside shelter and cut down two bystanders; when the Jiankang left district captain rushed to the scene, they hacked him as well.

sentences.zh: 隗劾嵩兄顗曰：「顗幸荷殊寵，列位上僚，當崇明憲典，協和上下，刑於左右，以禦於家邦。

translations.literal: Kui impeached Song's elder brother Yi, saying: "Yi has fortunately borne extraordinary favor, ranks among upper aides, ought to clarify and exalt the statutes and canons, harmonize above and below, model to left and right, thereby to regulate family and state.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui impeached Zhou Song's elder brother Zhou Yi: "Yi enjoys exceptional favor and sits among the highest ministers; he should exemplify the law, harmonize court and country, and set the tone for kin and household.

sentences.zh: 而乃縱肆小人，群為凶害，公於廣都之中白日刃尉，遠近洶嚇，百姓喧華，虧損風望，漸不可長。

translations.literal: Yet then he indulged petty men; a crowd became violent harm; in broad daylight in the broad capital he bladed the commandant; far and near roared in terror; the hundred surnames clamored; it injures and loses wind and reputation; gradually it cannot be allowed to grow.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he let petty followers run wild: in open day, in the capital's busiest streets, they drew steel on an officer of the law. The city shook with fear and public outcry; such damage to dignity cannot be left unchecked.

sentences.zh: 既無大臣檢禦之節，不可對揚休命。

translations.literal: Having neither the restraint and control of a great minister, he cannot face and extol glorious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He has shown none of the self-restraint expected of a senior statesman and is unfit to bear the emperor's glorious charge.

sentences.zh: 宜加貶黜，以肅其違。

translations.literal: It is fitting to add demotion and dismissal, to enforce his violation.
translations.idiomatic: He should be demoted to mark his offense and restore discipline.

sentences.zh: 」顗坐免官。

translations.literal: " Yi sat guilty and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Yi lost his post as a result.

sentences.zh: 太興初，長兼侍中，賜爵都鄉侯，尋代薛兼為丹陽尹，與尚書令刁協並為元帝所寵，欲排抑豪強。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixing, he was concurrent attendant-in-ordinary and was granted noble rank chief village marquis of Du; soon he replaced Xue Jian as Jiankang intendant; together with Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Diao Xie he was both favored by Emperor Yuan, wishing to suppress and check powerful magnates.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taixing he served as acting palace attendant and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Du; he soon succeeded Xue Jian as governor of the capital commandery. He and Diao Xie, the director of the secretariat, were Emperor Yuan's favorites, and together they set out to curb the great clans.

sentences.zh: 諸刻碎之政，皆云隗、協所建。

translations.literal: The various carved-petty policies, all said to be established by Kui and Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Every harsh, nitpicking reform was credited—or blamed—on Liu Kui and Diao Xie.

sentences.zh: 隗雖在外，萬機秘密皆豫聞之。

translations.literal: Though Kui was outside, the myriad affairs' secrets he all heard in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Even when Liu Kui held posts outside the palace, he was privy to every confidential decision at court.

sentences.zh: 拜鎮北將軍、都督青徐幽平四州軍事、假節，加散騎常侍，率萬人鎮泗口。

translations.literal: He was appointed general who guards the north, area commander for military affairs of Qing, Xu, You, and Ping four provinces, with credential; added cavalier attendant-in-ordinary; he led ten thousand men to garrison Sikou.
translations.idiomatic: He was named general who guards the north and military commander over Qing, Xu, You, and Ping, with imperial credentials, and given the additional title of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary; he took ten thousand troops to hold the Sikou crossing.

sentences.zh: 初，隗以王敦威權太盛，終不可制，勸帝出腹心以鎮方隅，故以譙王承為湘州，續用隗及戴若思為都督。

translations.literal: Initially, Kui because Wang Dun's awesomeness and power were too great, in the end could not be controlled, urged the emperor to dispatch trusted hearts to garrison the corners; therefore Prince of Qiao Cheng was made Xiangzhou; subsequently Kui and Dai Ruosi were used as area commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui had long warned that Wang Dun's power was too great to be checked; he urged the emperor to plant loyal commanders in the provinces—hence Prince Cheng of Qiao was sent to Xiangzhou, and Liu Kui himself and Dai Ruosi were later given regional commands.

sentences.zh: 敦甚惡之，與隗書曰：「頃承聖上顧眄足下，今大賊未滅，中原鼎沸，欲與足下周生之徒戮力王室，共靜海內。

translations.literal: Dun greatly hated it; he wrote Kui a letter saying: "Recently I have received that the sage superior gazes on you; now the great bandit is not yet destroyed, the central plain boils like a cauldron; I wish with you and the likes of Zhou Sheng to join strength in the royal house, together to quiet within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun detested the move and wrote to Liu Kui: "The emperor has been showing you uncommon favor. The great rebels are still abroad and the heartland is in turmoil; I had hoped that you, I, and men like Zhou would strain every nerve for the throne and bring peace back to the realm.

sentences.zh: 若其泰也，則帝祚於是乎隆；

translations.literal: If it is peaceful, then the imperial throne from this is prosperous;
translations.idiomatic: If we succeed, the dynasty will flourish again;

sentences.zh: 若其否也，則天下永無望矣。

translations.literal: if it is not, then under heaven there is forever no hope.
translations.idiomatic: if we fail, the empire may never recover.

sentences.zh: 」隗答曰：「魚相忘於江湖，人相忘於道術。

translations.literal: " Kui answered, saying: "Fish forget each other in rivers and lakes; people forget each other in the way and arts.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Kui replied: "Fish lose sight of one another once they reach the great rivers; true allies need no reminders when the Way is clear.

sentences.zh: 竭股肱之力，效之以忠貞，吾之志也。

translations.literal: To exhaust the strength of thigh and arm, to render it with loyalty and steadfastness—that is my aim.
translations.idiomatic: To give all I have as a loyal minister is precisely what I intend.

sentences.zh: 」敦得書甚怒。

translations.literal: " When Dun obtained the letter he was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun flew into a rage when he read the reply.

sentences.zh: 及敦作亂，以討隗為名，詔征隗還京師，百官迎之於道，隗岸幘大言，意氣自若。

translations.literal: When Dun raised rebellion, taking punishing Kui as pretext, an edict summoned Kui back to the capital; the hundred officials welcomed him on the road; Kui pushed up his headcloth and spoke loudly, spirit and bearing self-possessed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled under the slogan of punishing Liu Kui, an edict recalled Liu Kui to the capital; the whole bureaucracy turned out to greet him, and he marched in with his cap tilted back, declaiming boldly and showing not a trace of fear.

sentences.zh: 及入見，與刁協奏請誅王氏。

translations.literal: When he entered audience, together with Diao Xie he memorialized requesting to execute the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he joined Diao Xie in demanding the execution of the Wang family.

sentences.zh: 不從，有懼色，率眾屯金城。

translations.literal: It was not followed; he had a fearful look; he led a host and encamped at Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused; Liu Kui turned pale with fear and withdrew his troops to the Jincheng garrison.

sentences.zh: 及敦克石頭，隗攻之不拔，入宮告辭，帝雪涕與之別。

translations.literal: When Dun captured Stone Citadel, Kui attacked it but could not take it; he entered the palace to announce farewell; the emperor wiped tears and parted with him.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun seized Stone Citadel, Liu Kui's counterattack failed; he went to the palace to bid farewell, and the emperor wept as they parted.

sentences.zh: 隗至淮陰，為劉遐所襲，攜妻子及親信二百餘人奔于石勒，勒以為從事中郎、太子太傅。

translations.literal: When Kui reached Huaiyin, he was attacked by Liu Xia; carrying wife and children and more than two hundred trusted followers he fled to Shi Le; Le made him attendant gentleman for miscellaneous purposes and grand tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Near Huaiyin, Liu Xia ambushed him; Liu Kui fled with his family and some two hundred retainers to Shi Le's court, where he was given a staff post and the title of tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十一。

translations.literal: He died aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 子綏，初舉秀才，除駙馬都尉、奉朝請。

translations.literal: His son Sui, at first was recommended cultivated talent, was appointed chief commandant of carriages for the emperor's sons-in-law, attendant at court summons.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Sui first passed the provincial examination and was named chief commandant for imperial sons-in-law and gentleman attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 隨隗奔勒，卒。

translations.literal: Following Kui he fled to Le; died.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his father to Shi Le and died there.

sentences.zh: 孫波嗣。

translations.literal: Grandson Bo inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Sun Bo inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 波字道則。

translations.literal: Bo's courtesy name was Daize.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bo, courtesy name Daize.

sentences.zh: 初為石季龍冠軍將軍王洽參軍，及季龍死，洽與波俱降。

translations.literal: At first he was military adviser to Shi Jilong's general who champions the army Wang Qia; when Jilong died, Qia and Bo both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He first served on the staff of Wang Qia, general who champions the army under Shi Hu (Jilong); when Shi Hu died, Wang Qia and Sun Bo surrendered together.

sentences.zh: 穆帝以波為襄城太守，累遷桓沖中軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu made Bo Xiangcheng administrator; he was gradually promoted to Huan Chong's central army deliberation military adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu appointed him governor of Xiangcheng; he rose to become deliberation adviser on Huan Chong's central-army staff.

sentences.zh: 大司馬桓溫西征袁貞，朝廷空虛，以波為建威將軍、淮南內史，領五千人鎮石頭。

translations.literal: Grand marshal Huan Wen campaigned west against Yuan Zhen; the court was empty and weak; Bo was made general who establishes might, Huainan interior secretary, commanding five thousand men to garrison Stone Citadel.
translations.idiomatic: While Grand Marshal Huan Wen marched west against Yuan Zhen and the capital was stripped of troops, Sun Bo was named general who establishes might and interior secretary of Huainan, with five thousand men to hold Stone Citadel.

sentences.zh: 壽陽平，除尚書左丞，不拜，轉冠軍將軍、南郡相。

translations.literal: When Shouyang was pacified, he was appointed left aide to the Masters of Writing; he did not take office; was transferred to general who champions the army, Nan commandery chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Shouyang he was offered the post of left aide in the secretariat but declined it, and was reassigned as general who champions the army and administrator of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 時苻堅弟融圍雍州刺史硃序于襄陽，波率眾八千救之，以敵強不敢進，序竟陷沒。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Jian's younger brother Rong besieged Yongzhou inspector Zhu Xu at Xiangyang; Bo led a host of eight thousand to rescue him; because the enemy was strong he dared not advance; Xu in the end fell and was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Rong, Fu Jian's brother, besieged Zhu Xu, the Yongzhou governor, at Xiangyang, Sun Bo took eight thousand men to relieve him but halted before the enemy's strength; Zhu Xu was eventually captured.

sentences.zh: 波以畏懦免官。

translations.literal: Bo because of cowardice was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bo lost his post for timidity.

sentences.zh: 後復以波為冠軍將軍，累遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later again Bo was made general who champions the army; he was gradually promoted to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as general who champions the army and eventually promoted to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 苻堅敗，朝廷欲鎮靖北方，出波督淮北諸軍、冀州刺史，以疾未行。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was defeated, the court wished to pacify and quiet the north; Bo was sent out to supervise Huai north various armies, Ji province inspector; because of illness he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's defeat the court planned to stabilize the north and named Sun Bo commander of the armies north of the Huai and inspector of Ji, but illness kept him from taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He presented a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天地以弘濟為仁，君道以惠下為德，是以禹湯有身勤之績，唐虞有在予之誥，用能惠被蒼生，勳流後葉。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Heaven and Earth take broad succor as benevolence, and the way of the ruler takes kindness to those below as virtue; therefore Yu and Tang had the achievement of toil in person, Tang and Yu had the admonitions of 'it rests with me'; thereby they were able to extend kindness to the black-haired people and let merit flow to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: I have read that Heaven and Earth enshrine compassion in sustaining all life, and that a true king wins the realm by blessing his people—hence the tireless example of Yu and Tang and the self-reproaching words of Yao and Shun, until their grace reached every commoner and their fame lasted for ages.

sentences.zh: 宣帝開拓洪圖，始基成命；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan opened and expanded the great plan, began the foundation and completed the mandate;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Jin laid the vast foundations of the dynasty and set its mandate on solid ground;

sentences.zh: 爰及文武，歷數在躬，而猶虛心側席，卑己崇物。

translations.literal: down to Wen and Wu, the succession was in their persons, yet still they emptied their hearts and sat sideways on the mat, humbled themselves and honored others.
translations.idiomatic: his successors held the celestial mandate, yet still ruled with empty-minded humility, yielding the seat of honor and elevating wise men above themselves.

sentences.zh: 然後知積累之功重，勤王之業艱，先君之德弘，貽厥之賜厚。

translations.literal: Then one knows the achievement of accumulation is weighty, the enterprise of aiding the king is hard, the former lords' virtue is vast, the gift left to posterity is rich.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did people grasp how heavy a legacy must be, how arduous the work of restoring the throne, how great the virtue of the founding rulers, and how generous their bequest to later generations.

sentences.zh: 惠皇不懷，委政內任，遂使神器幽淪，三光翳曜；

translations.literal: Emperor Hui did not cherish it, entrusted government to inner favorites, so that the divine regalia sank into darkness, the three luminaries were eclipsed;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui neglected this charge, handed power to palace favorites, and the imperial throne sank into shadow while sun, moon, and stars seemed to lose their light;

sentences.zh: 園陵懷九泉之感，宮廟集胡馬之跡；

translations.literal: Imperial tombs harbored feelings of the nine springs; palace temples gathered the tracks of Hu horses;
translations.idiomatic: royal tombs echoed with the grief of the underworld, and barbarian horses trampled the ancestral shrines;

sentences.zh: 所謂肉食失之于朝，黎庶暴骸於外也。

translations.literal: What is called meat-eaters losing it at court, common folk exposing bones outside.
translations.idiomatic: the courtiers who fed at the public trough brought ruin in the capital while common people lay unburied in the fields.

sentences.zh: 賴元皇帝神武應期，祚隆淮海，振乾綱於已墜，紐絕維而更張。

translations.literal: Thanks to Emperor Yuan's divine martial responding to the season, fortune rose at Huai and sea, he raised the Heaven net already fallen, tied cut cords and restrung them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan answered the hour with martial vigor, rebuilt the dynasty on the Huai and the eastern sea, raised the sagging celestial net, and retied every broken strand of authority.

sentences.zh: 陛下承宣帝開始之宏基，受元帝克終之成烈，保大定功，戢兵靜亂。

translations.literal: Your Majesty inherits Emperor Xuan's beginning great foundation, receives Emperor Yuan's completing accomplished fierceness, preserves the great and fixes achievement, gathers weapons and quiets turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has inherited the grand design begun by Emperor Xuan and the finished work of Emperor Yuan; you have preserved the realm, sealed its victories, sheathed the armies, and stilled rebellion.

sentences.zh: 故使負鱗橫海之鯨，僭位滔天之寇，望雲旗而宵潰，睹太陽而霧散，巍巍蕩蕩，人無名焉。

translations.literal: Therefore caused scaly sea-spanning whales, usurping-position heaven-flooding bandits, to see cloud banners and flee by night, see the great sun and mist scatter, lofty and vast, men have no name for it.
translations.idiomatic: Whales that once lashed the waves and rebels who boasted they could swallow heaven melted away at sight of your banners and scattered like mist before the sun—so vast was the restoration that words fail.

sentences.zh: 而頃年已來，天文違錯，妖怪屢生。

translations.literal: Yet in recent years since, celestial patterns have been wrong and tangled, prodigies have repeatedly arisen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for some years now the sky has shown disorder, and strange portents have appeared again and again.

sentences.zh: 會稽先帝本封，而地動經年。

translations.literal: Kuaiji was the former emperor's original fief, yet the earth quaked for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji, the late emperor's first enfeoffment, has shaken with earthquakes for a year on end.

sentences.zh: 昔周之文武有魚烏之瑞，君臣猶懷震悚，況今災變眾集，曾莫之疑。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou's Wen and Wu had fish and crow auspices; ruler and ministers still harbored shock and fear; how much more now calamities and changes crowd together—yet there is no doubting of it.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wen and King Wu of Zhou received modest omens, the whole court still trembled; today calamities crowd upon us, yet no one seems alarmed.

sentences.zh: 公旦有勿休之誡，賈誼有積薪之喻。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou had the warning of do not rest; Jia Yi had the metaphor of piled firewood.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou warned that governance admits no rest; Jia Yi compared the state to firewood stacked to the rafters—one spark and it burns.

sentences.zh: 臣鑒先征，竊惟今事，是以敢肆狂瞽，直言無諱。

translations.literal: Your servant mirrors former precedents, privately considers present affairs; therefore dares unleash wild blindness, speak straight without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: I take my cue from past examples and weigh our present plight; though I am blind and rash, I beg leave to speak plainly and withhold nothing.

sentences.zh: 往者先帝以玄風禦世，責成群後，坐運天綱，隨化委順，故忘日計之功，收歲成之用。

translations.literal: Formerly the late emperor used dark wind to govern the age, entrusted tasks to the assembled lords, sat and moved the Heaven net, followed transformation and entrusted compliance; therefore forgot day-by-day achievement, gathered year-completed use.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor ruled through quiet, non-interfering ways, charged the great lords with duty, and let the cosmic pattern work itself out; he did not fuss over small daily gains but looked to harvests gathered once a year.

sentences.zh: 今禮樂征伐自天子出，相王賢俊，協和百揆，六合承風，天下響振，而鈞台之詠弗聞，景毫之命未布。

translations.literal: Now rites, music, punishments, and expeditions issue from the Son of Heaven; the minister-king is worthy and eminent, harmonizes the hundred directors; the six directions receive the wind, all under heaven echoes and trembles, yet the song of Jun Terrace is not heard, the mandate of Jing Bo is not proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Today ritual, music, war, and peace all proceed from the throne; the regent is wise, the ministries work in concert, and the realm answers like an echo—yet we do not hear the hymns of the ancient courts, nor see your transformative commands spread like those of Tang at Jing.

sentences.zh: 將群臣之不稱，陛不用之不盡乎？

translations.literal: Is it about the assembled ministers' not being suitable, or Your Majesty's not using them to the full?
translations.idiomatic: Is the fault in your ministers' unworthiness, or in the throne's failure to use their talents to the full?

sentences.zh: 凡聖王之化，莫不敦崇忠信，存正棄邪。

translations.literal: As for sage kings' transformation, none do not earnestly honor loyalty and trust, preserve the upright and discard the deviant.
translations.idiomatic: Every sage-king has exalted loyalty and good faith, upheld the right, and cast out the corrupt.

sentences.zh: 傷化毀俗者，雖親雖貴，必疏而遠之；

translations.literal: Those who injure transformation and destroy custom, though intimate though noble, must be kept distant and far;
translations.idiomatic: Those who corrupt morals, however high-born or well connected, must be pushed away;

sentences.zh: 清公貞修者，雖微雖賤，必親而近之。

translations.literal: Those who are pure, fair, chaste, and cultivated, though low though base, must be drawn near and kept close.
translations.idiomatic: the pure, upright, and self-disciplined, however humble, must be brought close.

sentences.zh: 今則不然。

translations.literal: Now it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Today the opposite holds.

sentences.zh: 此風既替，利競滋甚，朋黨比周，毀譽交興，鑽求苟進，人希分外。

translations.literal: This wind having declined, profit-seeking rivalry grows extreme, factions band together, slander and praise rise together, boring for advancement, people hope beyond their lot.
translations.idiomatic: That ethos has collapsed: greed and rivalry run wild, cliques smear and praise one another, men scheme for promotion, and everyone reaches for more than his due.

sentences.zh: 見賢而居其上，受祿每過其量，希旨承意者以為奉公，共相贊白者以為忠節。

translations.literal: Seeing the worthy yet sitting above them, receiving salary always exceeding their measure; those who hope for intent and carry out wishes are deemed to serve the public; those who mutually praise in white are deemed loyal and steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocrities lord it over their betters and draw salaries beyond their worth; flatterers who echo the court line pass for dutiful officials, and mutual back-scratching is mistaken for loyalty.

sentences.zh: 舉世見之，誰敢正言。

translations.literal: The whole age sees it; who dares speak straight?
translations.idiomatic: The whole world sees it, yet who dares speak plainly?

sentences.zh: 陛下不明必行之法以絕穿鑒之源者，恐脫因疲倦以誤視聽。

translations.literal: Your Majesty not clarifying laws that must be enforced to cut off the source of forced interpretation, I fear perhaps because of weariness to mistake seeing and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not spell out binding law to stop arbitrary rulings, I fear weariness may someday cloud your judgment.

sentences.zh: 且苻堅滅亡，於今五年，舊京殘毀，山陵無衛，百姓塗炭，未蒙拯接。

translations.literal: Moreover Fu Jian's destruction and death, to now five years; old capital ruined and destroyed, hills and tombs without guard; common people in mud and charcoal, have not received rescue and relief.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian fell five years ago, yet the old capital lies in ruins, imperial tombs stand undefended, and the people still burn in misery without relief.

sentences.zh: 伏願遠觀漢魏衰滅之由，近覽西朝傾覆之際，超然易慮，為於未有，則靈根永固，社稷無虞。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty from afar observe Han and Wei's decline and destruction's causes, near review Western dynasty's overturning's moment, transcendently change thought, act before there is yet; then the numinous root is forever firm, altars of soil and grain without worry.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to study why Han and Wei fell, to recall how the Western Jin collapsed, to shift course before crisis strikes—then the dynastic root will hold firm and the altars will face no peril.

sentences.zh: 臣豈誣一朝之人皆無忠節，但任非其才，求之不至耳。

translations.literal: How could your servant slander a court's people all lacking loyal steadfastness? Only appointment not matching their talent, seeking not reaching them.
translations.idiomatic: I do not claim that everyone at court lacks loyalty—only that the wrong men are given posts and true worth goes unsummoned.

sentences.zh: 今政煩役殷，所在凋弊，倉廩空虛，國用傾竭，下民侵削，流亡相屬。

translations.literal: Now government is vexing and corvée heavy, everywhere withered and exhausted, granaries empty and void, state use poured out and exhausted, people below encroached and cut, flight and wandering follow one another.
translations.idiomatic: Government is a tangle of orders, labor levies crush the districts, granaries are empty, the treasury is drained, commoners are bled white, and refugees trail one another on the roads.

sentences.zh: 略計戶口，但咸安已來，十分去三。

translations.literal: Roughly counting households, only since Xian'an, of ten parts three have gone.
translations.idiomatic: By a rough tally of households, nearly three in ten have vanished since the Xian'an era.

sentences.zh: 百姓懷浮游之歎，《下泉》興周京之思。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames harbor drifting wanderers' sighs; "Below the Spring" rouses Zhou capital's longing.
translations.idiomatic: The people sigh like rootless exiles; their mood is that of the ode "Below the Spring," longing for a capital made whole again.

sentences.zh: 昔漢宣有云：「與我共治天下者，其惟良二千石乎！

translations.literal: Formerly Han Xuan had words: "Those who with me jointly govern all under heaven—are they not the good two-thousand-shi?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han once said, "The men who truly share the empire with me are the worthy governors.

sentences.zh: 」是以臨下有方者就加璽贈，法苛政亂者恤刑不赦，事簡於上，人悅於下。

translations.literal: " Therefore those who rule those below with method were then added seal gifts; those whose law was harsh and government chaotic were shown pity in punishment without pardon; affairs were simple above, people pleased below.
translations.idiomatic: " So he ennobled magistrates who governed well, showed no mercy to cruel or chaotic rule, kept the court's business simple, and left the people content.

sentences.zh: 今則不然。

translations.literal: Now it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: None of that holds today.

sentences.zh: 告時乞職者以家弊為辭，振窮恤滯者以公爵為施。

translations.literal: Those who report times and beg office take family exhaustion as excuse; those who relieve the poor and pity the stuck take ducal rank as largesse.
translations.idiomatic: Men who angle for posts plead domestic hardship; those who would aid the needy hand out noble titles instead of real relief.

sentences.zh: 古者為百姓立君，使之司牧；

translations.literal: In antiquity for the hundred surnames they established a ruler, made him oversee and herd;
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity set a ruler over the people to shepherd them;

sentences.zh: 今者以百姓恤君，使之蠶食，至乃貪污者謂之清勤，慎法者謂之怯劣。

translations.literal: now they use the hundred surnames to pity the ruler, make them silkworm-eat, until even the greedy and corrupt are called pure and diligent, the law-cautious are called timid and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: now the people are milked to indulge the throne, gnawed away bit by bit; the grasping are praised as diligent, the law-abiding mocked as cowards.

sentences.zh: 何反古道一至於此！

translations.literal: How reverse the ancient way to reach this!
translations.idiomatic: How utterly we have inverted the ancient way!

sentences.zh: 陛下雖躬自節儉，哀矜於上，而群僚肆欲，縱心於下，六司垂翼，三事拱默，故有識者睹人事以歎息，觀妖眚而大懼。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty personally is frugal, pitying above, yet the host of officials indulge desire, give free rein to hearts below; the six bureaus hang wings, the three affairs arch in silence; therefore those with understanding seeing human affairs sigh, observing prodigies and calamities greatly fear.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty lives frugally and shows compassion above, but officials below indulge every appetite; the ministries fold their wings in silence, the three senior posts sit mute. Thoughtful men groan at these signs and tremble at each new portent.

sentences.zh: 昔宋景退熒惑之災，殷宗消鼎雉之異。

translations.literal: Formerly Song Jing retreated the Yinghuo disaster; Yin Zong dispelled tripod pheasant prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jing of Song averted Mars's curse by owning his fault; Emperor Gao of Yin quieted the cauldron-and-pheasant omen through self-reform.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下仰觀大禹過門之志，俯察商辛沈湎之失，遠思《國風》恭公之刺，深惟定薑小臣之喻。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty look up observe Great Yu's passing-the-gate resolve, look down examine Shang Xin's drowning-in-wine failure, far ponder the "Airs of the States" Duke Gong's satire, deeply consider Ding Jiang minor official's metaphor.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to recall Yu, who thrice passed his door without entering; to study the fall of Zhou's last king, lost to drink; to heed the Odes' warning against proud dukes; to weigh the lesson of Lady Ding Jiang's humble adviser.

sentences.zh: 暫回聖恩，大詢群後，延納眾賢，訪以得失；

translations.literal: Briefly turn sage grace, greatly consult the assembled lords, extend and receive the host of worthies, inquire of them gain and loss;
translations.idiomatic: Pause, extend your grace, consult the great lords broadly, summon worthy men, and ask where policy has failed or succeeded;

sentences.zh: 令百僚率職，人言損益。

translations.literal: order the hundred officials each perform duty, each person speak harm and benefit.
translations.idiomatic: require every official to perform his role and speak plainly about what helps or harms the state.

sentences.zh: 察其所由，觀其所以，審識群才，助鼎和味。

translations.literal: Examine whence they come, observe whereby they are so, carefully know the host of talents, help the tripod harmonize flavors.
translations.idiomatic: Probe how men behave, judge their motives, know each talent for what it is, and blend them like seasonings in the royal cauldron.

sentences.zh: 克念作聖，以答天休。

translations.literal: Able to think, become sage, thereby answer Heaven's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Hold fast to right intent and you become sage-king, worthy of Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 則四海宅心，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Then within the four seas hearts take dwelling; all under heaven is greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Then the realm will find its heart in you, and all the world will be the better for it.

sentences.zh: 臣亡祖先臣隗，昔荷殊寵，匪躬之操，猶存舊史，有志無時，懷恨黃泉。

translations.literal: Your servant's deceased grandfather former subject Kui, formerly bore extraordinary favor; not-self body's conduct, still exists in old histories; had aspiration without season, harbored regret in the yellow springs.
translations.idiomatic: My late grandfather Liu Kui once enjoyed rare favor and gave his all for the throne—his story still lives in the histories—yet the hour never matched his will, and he carried grievance to the grave.

sentences.zh: 及臣凡劣，復蒙罔極之眷，恩隆累世，實非糜身傾宗所能上報。

translations.literal: As for your servant mean and inferior, again receiving boundless favor, grace lofty for accumulated generations, truly is not what grinding body and overturning clan can repay above.
translations.idiomatic: I am a lesser man, yet I too have received bottomless kindness, generation upon generation—no sacrifice of life or house could repay it.

sentences.zh: 前作此表，未及得通。

translations.literal: Previously composing this memorial, did not reach being passed through.
translations.idiomatic: I drafted this memorial once before but it never reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 暴嬰篤疾，恐命在奄忽，貪及視息，望達愚情。

translations.literal: Suddenly stricken with serious illness, fearing life is in sudden passing, greedily reaching while yet breathing and seeing, hope to convey foolish feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden grave illness may cut me off at any moment; while I still draw breath I crave only to make my humble plea heard.

sentences.zh: 氣力懾然，不能自宣。

translations.literal: Breath and strength trembling, unable to declare himself.
translations.idiomatic: My strength fails; I can scarcely give it voice.

sentences.zh: 疏奏而卒。

translations.literal: The memorial was presented and he died.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, and he died.

sentences.zh: 追贈前將軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted general of the van.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as general of the van.

sentences.zh: 子淡嗣。

translations.literal: His son Dan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Dan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 元熙初，為廬江太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxi, he was Lujiang administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanxi he became governor of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 隗伯父訥，字令言，有人倫鑒識。

translations.literal: Kui's paternal uncle Ne, courtesy name Lingyan, had human-relations mirror insight.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui's uncle Liu Ne, courtesy name Lingyan, was a shrewd judge of character.

sentences.zh: 初入洛，見諸名士而歎曰：「王夷甫太鮮明，樂彥輔我所敬，張茂先我所不解，周弘武巧於用短，杜方叔拙于用長。

translations.literal: When he first entered Luoyang, seeing the various famous gentlemen he sighed, saying: "Wang Yifu is too bright and clear; Yue Yanfu is one I respect; Zhang Maoxian is one I do not understand; Zhou Hongwu is clever in using the short; Du Fangshu is clumsy in using the long.
translations.idiomatic: On his first visit to Luoyang he sized up the leading lights and remarked: "Wang Yan shines too brightly; I esteem Yue Guang; I cannot fathom Zhang Hua; Zhou Yi turns his faults to advantage; Du Yu squanders his strengths.

sentences.zh: 」終於司隸校尉。

translations.literal: " He ended as metropolitan commandant.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in office as metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 子疇，字王喬，少有美譽，善談名理。

translations.literal: His son Chou, courtesy name Wangqiao, in youth had fine reputation, skilled at discussing name principles.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Chou, courtesy name Wangqiao, won early renown and excelled at Pure Conversation.

sentences.zh: 曾避亂塢壁，賈胡百數欲害之，疇無懼色，援笳而吹之，為《出塞》、《入塞》之聲，以動其遊客之思。

translations.literal: Once fleeing turmoil in a fortified village, foreign merchants by the hundred wished to harm him; Chou had no fear, took up a reed pipe and blew it, making "Out of the Pass" and "Into the Pass" sounds, to move their wandering guests' thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Once, sheltering from war in a walled hamlet, he faced hundreds of Sogdian traders bent on killing him; he showed no fear, lifted a reed whistle, and played the old frontier tunes "Out of the Pass" and "Into the Pass," stirring their homesickness.

sentences.zh: 於是群胡皆垂泣而去之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the host of Hu all wept and left him.
translations.idiomatic: The merchants wept and went away without harming him.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，位至司徒左長史，尋為閻鼎所殺。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia era, his position reached steward's left chief clerk; soon was killed by Yan Ding.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongjia he rose to senior clerk on the minister of education's staff and was soon murdered by Yan Ding.

sentences.zh: 司空蔡謨每歎曰：「若使劉王喬得南渡，司徒公之美選也。

translations.literal: Minister of works Cai Mo often sighed, saying: "If Liu Wangqiao had been able to cross south, he would have been the steward duke's fine selection.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo, minister of works, used to sigh, "Had Liu Wangqiao reached the south, he would have been the perfect choice for minister of education.

sentences.zh: 」又王導初拜司徒，謂人曰：「劉王喬若過江，我不獨拜公也。

translations.literal: " Also when Wang Dao first was appointed steward, he told people: "If Liu Wangqiao had crossed the river, I would not alone have been appointed duke.
translations.idiomatic: " When Wang Dao first took the seal of minister of education, he said, "If Liu Wangqiao had crossed the Yangzi, I would not stand here alone as grandee.

sentences.zh: 」其為名流之所推服如此。

translations.literal: " Such was he whom the famous current pushed and served.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem the elite accorded him.

sentences.zh: 疇兄子劭，有才幹，辟琅邪王丞相掾。

translations.literal: Chou's elder brother's son Shao, had talent and capacity, was summoned as Langye Wang's chief minister aide.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao, nephew of Liu Chou, was capable and was called to serve on the Prince of Langye's chief-minister staff.

sentences.zh: 咸康世，曆御史中丞、侍中、尚書、豫章太守，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: In the Xiankang era, he passed through vice censor-in-chief, attendant-in-ordinary, Masters of Writing, Yuzhang administrator, rank two thousand shi at middle.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiankang he served successively as vice censor-in-chief, palace attendant, ministerial secretary, and governor of Yuzhang at the two-thousand-shi rank.

sentences.zh: 邵族子黃老，太元中，為尚書郎，有義學，注《慎子》、《老子》，並傳於世。

translations.literal: Shao's clansman Huanglao, in the Taiyuan era, was Masters of Writing gentleman, had moral learning, annotated "Shenzi" and "Laozi," both transmitted in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's kinsman Huanglao served as a secretary at the secretariat during Taiyuan; he was a scholar of moral philosophy and produced commentaries on the Shenzi and Laozi that still circulate.

sentences.zh: 協性剛悍，與物多忤，每崇上抑下，故為王氏所疾。

translations.literal: Xie by nature was fierce and harsh, with things often clashed, always exalting superiors and suppressing inferiors; therefore was resented by the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie was truculent and abrasive, forever flattering those above and riding roughshod over those below; the Wang clan loathed him for it.

sentences.zh: 又使酒放肆，侵毀公卿，見者莫不側目。

translations.literal: Also when drunk was wanton, encroached on and slandered dukes and ministers; those who witnessed it all glared sidelong.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he insulted the great officers of state so openly that onlookers could only glare sideways.

sentences.zh: 然悉力盡心，志在匡救，帝甚信任之。

translations.literal: Yet he exhausted strength and heart, aspiration lay in aiding and saving; the emperor greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he gave everything to right the realm, and the emperor placed deep trust in him.

sentences.zh: 以奴為兵，取將吏客使轉運，皆協所建也，眾庶怨望之。

translations.literal: Using slaves as soldiers, taking generals' clerks' retainers to make transport—all were established by Xie; the multitude resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Conscripting bond servants as soldiers, pressing generals' clerks and their clients into convoy duty—these were Diao Xie's policies, and the people cursed him for them.

sentences.zh: 及王敦構逆，上疏罪協。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun framed rebellion, he submitted a memorial blaming Xie.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled, his first memorial named Diao Xie as the villain.

sentences.zh: 帝使協出督六軍。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Xie out to supervise the six armies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Diao Xie out to command the six hosts.

sentences.zh: 既而王師敗績，協與劉隗俱侍帝於太極東除，帝執協、隗手，流涕嗚咽，勸令避禍。

translations.literal: Soon the royal army was defeated; Xie together with Liu Kui both attended the emperor at Taichi east steps; the emperor grasped Xie's and Kui's hands, wept tears and sobbed, urged them to avoid calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army broke, Diao Xie and Liu Kui stood with the emperor on the eastern steps of the Taichi Hall; he took their hands, weeping, and begged them to flee and save themselves.

sentences.zh: 協曰：「臣當守死，不敢有貳。

translations.literal: Xie said: "Your servant ought to guard unto death, dare not have two minds.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie replied, "I should die at my post; I would never turn disloyal.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「今事逼矣，安可不行！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Now affairs press; how can you not go!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Matters have gone too far—you must go!

sentences.zh: 」乃令給協、隗人馬，使自為計。

translations.literal: " Thereupon ordered to supply Xie and Kui men and horses, let them plan for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gave Diao Xie and Liu Kui mounts and escorts and told them to make their own way to safety.

sentences.zh: 協年老，不堪騎乘，素無恩紀，募從者，皆委之行。

translations.literal: Xie was old, could not bear riding; plain lack of kindness and discipline; summoned followers, all abandoned him and went.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie was too old to ride, had never won men's loyalty, and every follower he recruited slipped away and left him.

sentences.zh: 至江乘，為人所殺，送首於敦，敦德刁氏，收葬之。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiangcheng, he was killed by someone; the head was sent to Dun; Dun was grateful to the Diao clan, gathered and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangcheng assassins cut him down and sent his head to Wang Dun, who—mindful of old ties to the Diao family—had the body gathered and buried.

sentences.zh: 帝痛協不免，密捕送協首者而誅之。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved Xie could not be spared, secretly arrested the one who sent Xie's head and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned Diao Xie's fate and secretly seized the man who had delivered his head and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 敦平後，周顗、戴若思等皆被顯贈，惟協以出奔不在其例。

translations.literal: After Dun was pacified, Zhou Yi, Dai Ruosi, and others all received manifest posthumous gifts; only Xie because of fleeing out was not within the precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun's defeat, Zhou Yi, Dai Ruosi, and others received posthumous honors; Diao Xie alone was excluded because he had fled.

sentences.zh: 咸康中，協子彝上疏訟之。

translations.literal: In the Xiankang era, Xie's son Yi submitted a memorial suing for it.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiankang his son Diao Yi petitioned for redress.

sentences.zh: 在位者多以明帝之世褒貶已定，非所得更議，且協不能抗節隕身，乃出奔遇害，不可復其官爵也。

translations.literal: Those in office mostly held that in Emperor Ming's age praise and blame were already fixed, not what could be further debated; moreover Xie could not resist integrity and destroy body, then fled out and met harm; it is not possible to restore his office and noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Most officials argued that Emperor Ming had already settled Diao Xie's verdict and that it should not be reopened; besides, he had not died resisting the rebels but had fled and been killed en route—his titles could not be restored.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹殷融議曰：「王敦惡逆，罪不容誅，則協之善亦不容賞。

translations.literal: Danyang intendant Yin Rong deliberated, saying: "Wang Dun was wicked and rebellious; his guilt exceeded what execution could answer—therefore Xie's good likewise cannot bear reward.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Rong, governor of Danyang, argued: "Wang Dun's treason was so grave that death alone could not settle the account; in that setting Diao Xie's loyalty cannot be crowned with honors without contradiction."

sentences.zh: 若以忠非良圖，謀事失算，以此為責者，蓋在於譏議之間耳。

translations.literal: If because loyalty was not good plan, planning affairs missed calculation, taking this as blame—lies between ridicule and discussion.
translations.idiomatic: If one faults him for misguided loyalty or poor planning, that is a matter for moral debate, not capital law.

sentences.zh: 即凶殘之誅以為國刑，將何以沮勸乎！

translations.literal: Then taking cruel slaughter as state punishment—how will thereby discourage and encourage!
translations.idiomatic: To treat his killers' cruelty as lawful execution—what lesson would that teach loyalty or treason?

sentences.zh: 當敦專逼之時，慶賞威刑專自己出，是以元帝慮深崇本，以協為比，事由國計，蓋不為私。

translations.literal: When Dun monopolized pressure, rewards and punishments issued from himself alone; therefore Emperor Yuan's concern was deep and honored the root, took Xie as aide—affairs stemmed from state plan, in general was not for private ends.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Dun held the capital hostage, reward and terror alike came from his hand alone; Emperor Yuan therefore looked to the foundations of state and relied on Diao Xie—all for the dynasty, not private interest.

sentences.zh: 昔孔甯、儀行父從君于昏，楚復其位者，君之黨故也。

translations.literal: Formerly Kong Ning and Yi Hangfu followed the ruler in darkness; Chu restored their positions because they were the ruler's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ning and Yi Hangfu debauched their lord, yet Chu restored their offices because they were the king's own faction.

sentences.zh: 況協之比君，在於義順。

translations.literal: How much more Xie's relation to the ruler lay in righteousness and compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie's service to the throne was loyal and rightful by any measure.

sentences.zh: 且中興四佐，位為朝首。

translations.literal: Moreover the restoration's four assistants, rank was court head.
translations.idiomatic: He was one of the four chief ministers who rebuilt the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 于時事窮計屈，奉命違寇，非為逃刑。

translations.literal: At that time affairs were exhausted and plans bent; receiving mandate fleeing the bandit, was not to escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When every stratagem had failed, he obeyed the emperor's order to quit the rebel-held capital—not to dodge justice.

sentences.zh: 謂宜顯贈，以明忠義。

translations.literal: I say it is fitting to manifest posthumous gifts, thereby clarify loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He deserves a clear posthumous honor so the world may see what loyalty means.

sentences.zh: 」時庾冰輔政，疑不能決。

translations.literal: " At that time Yu Bing assisted government, doubted and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Bing, then regent, hesitated and left the matter unsettled.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫蔡謨與冰書曰：

translations.literal: Left household grandee Cai Mo wrote Bing a letter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo, left household grandee, wrote to Yu Bing:

sentences.zh: 夫爵人者，宜顯其功；

translations.literal: As for ennobling people, it is fitting to manifest their merit;
translations.idiomatic: When you enfeoff a man, you proclaim his merit;

sentences.zh: 罰人者，宜彰其罪，此古今之所慎也。

translations.literal: punishing people, it is fitting to display their guilt; this is what antiquity and present are cautious about.
translations.idiomatic: when you punish him, you publish his crime—ages past and present have treated both with care.

sentences.zh: 凡小之人猶尚如此，刁令中興上佐，有死難之名，天下不聞其罪，而見其貶，致令刁氏稱冤，此乃為王敦復仇也。

translations.literal: As for petty people still are thus; Minister Diao was restoration upper aide, had die-in-calamity's name; all under heaven did not hear his guilt, yet saw his demotion, causing the Diao clan to call wrong—this is thereby to avenge Wang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Even common folk grasp that principle. Diao Xie was a pillar of the restoration and died in the emperor's service; the realm never heard him judged guilty, yet it sees him disgraced while the Diao family cries injustice—that would be doing Wang Dun's vengeful work for him.

sentences.zh: 內沮忠臣之節，論者惑之。

translations.literal: Within discouraging loyal ministers' steadfastness, discussers are confused by it.
translations.idiomatic: It would break the spirit of loyal ministers and leave every commentator baffled.

sentences.zh: 若實有大罪，宜顯其事，令天下知之，明聖朝不貶死難之臣。

translations.literal: If he truly had great guilt, it is fitting to make manifest the affair, let all under heaven know it, clarify that the sage court does not demean ministers who died in its service.
translations.idiomatic: If he was truly guilty, publish the facts so the realm may judge, and show that this court does not dishonor men who died for their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，以功補過。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn's principle uses merit to offset fault.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals teach that merit may redeem fault.

sentences.zh: 過輕功重者，得以加封；

translations.literal: Where fault is light and merit heavy, enfeoffment may be added;
translations.idiomatic: Light offense and heavy service may earn a new title;

sentences.zh: 功輕過重者，不免誅絕；

translations.literal: where merit is light and fault heavy, execution and extirpation cannot be avoided;
translations.idiomatic: slight service and grave fault still merit death and the cutting off of the line;

sentences.zh: 功足贖罪者無黜。

translations.literal: where merit suffices to redeem crime, there is no dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: when service outweighs crime, the man need not be cast out.

sentences.zh: 雖先有邪佞之罪，而臨難之日党於其君者，不絕之也。

translations.literal: Although they earlier had deviant and fawning guilt, yet on the day of facing calamity they sided with their ruler—they are not cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Even men once corrupt who, when disaster struck, stood by their king were not written off forever.

sentences.zh: 孔甯、儀行父親與靈公淫亂於朝，君殺國滅，由此二臣，而楚尚納之。

translations.literal: Kong Ning and Yi Hangfu personally with Duke Ling debauched the court; the ruler was killed and the state destroyed—because of these two ministers—yet Chu still accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ning and Yi Hangfu debauched Duke Ling of Chen in open court; the duke died and the state fell—yet Chu still took them in.

sentences.zh: 傳稱有禮不絕其位者，君之黨也。

translations.literal: The commentary says there are cases where ritual does not cut off their positions—they were the ruler's faction.
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says some men keep rank despite scandal when they belong to the ruler's own party.

sentences.zh: 若刁令有罪，重于孔儀，絕之可也。

translations.literal: If Minister Diao's guilt were heavier than Kong's and Yi's, cutting him off would be permissible.
translations.idiomatic: If Diao Xie's crimes outweighed those of Kong Ning and Yi Hangfu, disowning him would be fair.

sentences.zh: 若無此罪，宜見追論。

translations.literal: If there is not this guilt, it is fitting to see posthumous reappraisal.
translations.idiomatic: If no such guilt exists, he deserves a formal reassessment.

sentences.zh: 或謂明帝之世已見寢廢，今不宜復改，吾又以為不然。

translations.literal: Some say in Emperor Ming's age it was already tabled and abandoned, now it is not fitting to change again—I also think this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue Emperor Ming settled the case and it should not be reopened—I disagree.

sentences.zh: 夫大道宰世，殊塗一致。

translations.literal: As for the great way governing the age, different paths are one in principle.
translations.idiomatic: The great Way rules the world; many roads lead to the same end.

sentences.zh: 萬機之事，或異或同，同不相善，異不相譏。

translations.literal: Of the myriad threads of business, some differ and some agree; agreement does not mean mutual praise, difference does not mean mutual ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs of state may match or clash across reigns; agreement need not mean approval, difference need not mean censure.

sentences.zh: 故堯抑元凱而舜舉之，堯不為失，舜不為非，何必前世所廢便不宜改乎？

translations.literal: Therefore Yao restrained the Yuan and Kai yet Shun raised them—Yao was not wrong, Shun was not improper—why must what a former age abolished be unfit to change?
translations.idiomatic: Yao sidelined certain men and Shun promoted them—neither was wrong. Why treat every past verdict as final?

sentences.zh: 漢蕭何之後坐法失侯，文帝不封而景帝封之，後復失侯，武昭二帝不封而宣帝封之。

translations.literal: In Han, Xiao He's later line lost its marquisate for violating law; Emperor Wen did not re-enfeoff but Emperor Jing did; later again lost the marquisate; Emperors Wu and Zhao did not re-enfeoff but Emperor Xuan did.
translations.idiomatic: Han history shows Xiao He's heirs lost their fief to a legal fault—Wen withheld restoration, Jing granted it; they lost it again, and later emperors debated the same question until Xuan restored them.

sentences.zh: 近去元年，車駕釋奠，拜孔子之坐，此亦元明二帝所不行也。

translations.literal: Recently, in the first year, the imperial carriage performed the capping sacrifice and bowed at Confucius's seat—this also Yuan and Ming two emperors did not do.
translations.idiomatic: Only last year the court offered wine to Confucius—a rite neither Emperor Yuan nor Emperor Ming had performed.

sentences.zh: 又刁令但是明帝所不贈耳，非誅之也。

translations.literal: Moreover Minister Diao was only what Emperor Ming did not posthumously ennoble, not what was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming merely withheld honors from Diao Xie; he did not condemn him as a criminal.

sentences.zh: 王平子、第五猗皆元帝所誅，而今日所贈，豈以改前為嫌乎！

translations.literal: Wang Pingzi and Di Wuyi were both executed by Emperor Yuan, yet today they receive posthumous gifts—is revising an earlier judgment therefore taboo?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan executed Wang Cheng and Di Wuyi, yet both have since been honored—why should Diao Xie alone be frozen in an old slight?

sentences.zh: 凡處事者，當上合古義，下准今例，然後談者不惑，受罪者無怨耳。

translations.literal: Generally those who handle affairs ought above accord with ancient meaning, below align with present precedent—then discussers are not confused and those who suffer punishment harbor no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Sound policy looks to antiquity and to current precedent alike; then the debate stays clear and the punished feel justice was done.

sentences.zh: 案周僕射、戴征西本非王敦唱檄所仇也，事定後乃見害耳；

translations.literal: Investigating: Household steward Zhou and west expedition Dai were originally not those Wang Dun's proclamation denounced; after affairs settled they were then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Privy counselor Zhou Yi and western commander Dai Yuan were not named in Wang Dun's manifesto; they were murdered only after peace returned.

sentences.zh: 周筵、郭璞等並亦非為主禦難也，自平居見殺耳，皆見褒贈，刁令事義豈輕於此乎？

translations.literal: Zhou Yan, Guo Pu, and others likewise were not defending the ruler against calamity; in ordinary times they were killed—all received praise and posthumous gifts; can Minister Diao's case in righteousness be lighter than this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yan and Guo Pu were not even dying in battle for the throne—they were cut down in peacetime—yet both were eulogized. Diao Xie's loyalty weighs no less.

sentences.zh: 自頃員外散騎尚得追贈，況刁令位亞三司。

translations.literal: Recently even supernumerary cavalier attendants have obtained posthumous enfeoffment; how much more Minister Diao, whose rank neighbored the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Lately even honorary cavaliers win posthumous titles; Diao Xie stood just below the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 若先自壽終，不失員外散騎之例也。

translations.literal: If he had first died a natural death, he would not have fallen below the precedent for supernumerary cavalier attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Had he died in bed, he would at least have matched the honors due a supernumerary gentleman.

sentences.zh: 就不蒙贈，不失以本官殯葬也。

translations.literal: Even if he did not receive posthumous gifts, he would not have lost burial according to his substantive office.
translations.idiomatic: Even without posthumous promotion, he would still merit burial befitting his rank.

sentences.zh: 此為一人之身，壽終則蒙贈，死難則見絕，豈所以明事君之道，厲為臣之節乎！

translations.literal: Here is one man's body: if he ends life naturally then he receives posthumous gifts; if he dies in calamity then he is cut off—is this the way to clarify the way of serving a ruler and encourage ministers' steadfastness!
translations.idiomatic: The same man would be honored for dying in bed but disowned for dying for the throne—how does that teach loyalty?

sentences.zh: 宜顯評其事，以解天下疑惑之論。

translations.literal: It is fitting openly to judge the affair, thereby to dispel the doubtful discussions of all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Publish a clear ruling and lay the realm's doubts to rest.

sentences.zh: 又聞談者亦多謂宜贈。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear among discussers many also say it is fitting to enfeoff.
translations.idiomatic: I hear most informed opinion favors restoration.

sentences.zh: 凡事不允當，而得眾助者，若以善柔得眾，而刁令粗剛多怨；

translations.literal: In general when affairs are not apt yet gain the multitude's aid—if it were by kindness and softness gaining the multitude, yet Minister Diao was rough and stiff and had many resentments;
translations.idiomatic: When an unpopular cause still wins support, it is not because the man was sweet-tempered—Diao Xie was blunt and widely resented;

sentences.zh: 若以貴也，刁氏今賤；

translations.literal: if it were by nobility, the Diao clan is now base;
translations.idiomatic: it is not birth: the Diaos are now humble;

sentences.zh: 若以富也，刁氏今貧。

translations.literal: if it were by wealth, the Diao clan is now poor.
translations.idiomatic: it is not wealth: they are ruined.

sentences.zh: 人士何故反助寒門而此言之？

translations.literal: Why then do gentlemen conversely aid cold gates and speak thus?
translations.idiomatic: Why should elite opinion side with the powerless in urging this?

sentences.zh: 足下宜察此意。

translations.literal: You ought to examine this meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Consider what that implies.

sentences.zh: 冰然之。

translations.literal: Bing assented.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing accepted the argument.

sentences.zh: 事奏，成帝詔曰：「協情在忠主，而失為臣之道，故令王敦得託名公義，而實肆私忌，遂令社稷受屈，元皇銜恥，致禍之原，豈不有由！

translations.literal: The affair was presented; Emperor Cheng's edict said: "Xie's feeling lay in loyally serving the ruler, yet he lost the way of being a minister; therefore he let Wang Dun borrow public righteousness in name while in reality indulging private jealousy, thereby causing the altars of soil and grain to suffer wrong, Emperor Yuan to bear shame—the origin of bringing calamity, how could there be no cause!
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went up; Emperor Cheng decreed: "Diao Xie's heart was loyal, but he failed as a minister, giving Wang Dun a pretext to rebel while nursing private spite—thus the state suffered and Emperor Yuan was humiliated. That disaster had roots.

sentences.zh: 若極明國典，則曩刑非重。

translations.literal: If one exhaustively clarifies state canons, then the former punishment was not heavy.
translations.idiomatic: By the strict letter of law his earlier treatment was not excessive.

sentences.zh: 今正當以協之勤有可書，敦之逆命不可長，故議其事耳。

translations.literal: Now it is just that because Xie's diligence is worth recording, and Dun's defiance of mandate cannot be prolonged, therefore we deliberate this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his service deserves record, and Wang Dun's treason cannot be the last word—hence this review.

sentences.zh: 今可復協本位，加之冊祭，以明有忠於君者纖介必顯，雖於貶裁未盡，然或足有勸矣。

translations.literal: Now we may restore Xie's original rank, add document and sacrifice, thereby to clarify that those loyal to the ruler, however slight, must be manifest; though in demotion and cutting it was not exhaustive, yet perhaps it suffices to have encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Restore his former office, grant him documented sacrifice, and show that loyalty to the throne, however slight, will out—even if the earlier demotion was not fully reversed, the example will encourage others.

sentences.zh: 」於是追贈本官，祭乙太牢。

translations.literal: " Thereupon posthumously gifted his original office, sacrificed with great beast offering.
