translations.idiomatic: " The court restored his titles and offered him the great beast sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 彝字大倫。

translations.literal: Yi's courtesy name was Dalun.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yi, courtesy name Dalun.

sentences.zh: 少遭家難。

translations.literal: In youth he encountered family disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered family tragedy while young.

sentences.zh: 王敦誅後，彝斬仇人党，以首祭父墓，詣廷尉請罪，朝廷特宥之，由是知名，曆尚書吏部郎、吳國內史，累遷北中郎將、徐兗二州刺史、假節，鎮廣陵，卒於官。

translations.literal: After Wang Dun was executed, Yi beheaded his enemy's faction, used the heads to sacrifice at his father's tomb, went to the commandant of justice to confess guilt; the court specially pardoned him; from this he became known; he passed through Masters of Writing personnel gentleman, Wu interior secretary, was gradually promoted to north general of the household gentlemen, Xu and Yan two provinces' inspector, with credential, garrisoned Guangling, died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun's death Diao Yi slew his father's killers, presented their heads at the tomb, then surrendered to justice; the court pardoned him and he rose to fame, serving as personnel director, governor of Wu, then general of the household gentlemen in the north and inspector of Xu and Yan with a garrison at Guangling, where he died in post.

sentences.zh: 子逵，字伯道，逵弟暢，字仲遠；

translations.literal: His son Kui, courtesy name Bodao; Kui's younger brother Chang, courtesy name Zhongyuan;
translations.idiomatic: His son Diao Kui, courtesy name Bodao, and younger son Diao Chang, courtesy name Zhongyuan;

sentences.zh: 次子弘，字叔仁，並曆顯職。

translations.literal: second son Hong, courtesy name Shuren, all passed through eminent offices.
translations.idiomatic: a second son, Diao Hong, courtesy name Shuren—all rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 隆安中，達為廣州刺史，領平越中郎將、假節；

translations.literal: In Long'an, Kui was Guangzhou inspector, concurrently general of the household gentlemen who pacifies the Yue, with credential;
translations.idiomatic: During Long'an, Diao Kui was inspector of Guangzhou and general who pacifies the Yue, with imperial credentials;

sentences.zh: 暢為始興相；

translations.literal: Chang was Shixing chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Diao Chang was administrator of Shixing;

sentences.zh: 弘為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Hong was Ji province inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Hong was inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 兄弟子侄並不拘名行，以貨殖為務，有田萬頃，奴婢數千人，餘資稱是。

translations.literal: Brothers, sons, and nephews all did not bind themselves to reputation and conduct; they took mercantile gain as their task; they had ten thousand qing of fields, several thousand slaves and maids, remaining assets matching this.
translations.idiomatic: The clan cared little for reputation; they chased profit, owned myriad hectares, thousands of bond servants, and fortunes to match.

sentences.zh: 桓玄篡位，以逵為西中郎將、豫州刺史，鎮曆陽；

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, he appointed Kui as west general of the household gentlemen, Yu province inspector, garrisoned Liyang;
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan seized the throne he named Diao Kui western general of the household gentlemen and inspector of Yu, stationed at Liyang;

sentences.zh: 暢右衛將軍；

translations.literal: Chang as general of the right guard;
translations.idiomatic: Diao Chang as general of the right guard;

sentences.zh: 弘撫軍桓修司馬。

translations.literal: Hong as army supervisor Huan Xiu's major.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Hong as major to the army supervisor Huan Xiu.

sentences.zh: 劉裕起義，斬桓修，時暢、弘謀起兵襲裕，裕遣劉毅討之，暢伏誅；

translations.literal: When Liu Yu raised righteous arms and beheaded Huan Xiu, at that time Chang and Hong plotted to raise troops to strike Yu; Yu sent Liu Yi to punish them; Chang was executed by ambush;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu rose against Huan Xiu and killed him, Diao Chang and Diao Hong plotted a counterstroke; Liu Yu sent Liu Yi against them; Chang was captured and executed;

sentences.zh: 弘亡，不知所在。

translations.literal: Hong fled; his whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Hong vanished without trace.

sentences.zh: 逵在曆陽執劉裕參軍諸葛長民，檻車送于桓玄，至當利而玄敗，送人共破檻出長民，遂趣曆陽。

translations.literal: Kui at Liyang seized Liu Yu's military adviser Zhuge Changmin, caged cart sent him to Huan Xuan; reaching Dangli Xuan was defeated; the escorts together broke the cage and released Changmin, then hastened to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Kui at Liyang seized Liu Yu's aide Zhuge Changmin and sent him toward Huan Xuan in a prison cart; near Dangli Xuan fell; the guards freed Changmin and raced back to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 逵棄城而走，為下人所執，斬於石頭。

translations.literal: Kui abandoned the city and fled, was seized by inferiors, beheaded at Stone Citadel.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Kui fled the city, was caught by his own men, and executed at Stone Citadel.

sentences.zh: 子侄無少長皆死，惟小弟騁被宥，為給事中，尋謀反伏誅，刁氏遂滅。

translations.literal: Sons and nephews without regard to young or old all died; only the youngest brother Cheng received pardon, became palace service gentleman; soon plotted rebellion and was executed; the Diao clan was thereby extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Every adult kinsman died; only the youngest brother Diao Cheng was spared as a palace attendant, then rebelled and was killed—the Diaos were gone.

sentences.zh: 刁氏素殷富，奴客縱橫，固吝山澤，為京口之蠹。

translations.literal: The Diao clan had long been opulently rich; retainers and clients ran rampant, stubbornly monopolizing hills and marshes, becoming the canker of Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the Diaos had hoarded wealth, bullied the countryside, and monopolized Jingkou's hills and streams.

sentences.zh: 裕散其資蓄，今百姓稱力而取之，彌日不盡。

translations.literal: Yu scattered their stored wealth, ordered the hundred surnames to take according to their strength; a full day did not exhaust it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu broke open their granaries and let commoners carry away what they could; a day was not enough to empty them.

sentences.zh: 時天下饑弊，編戶賴之以濟焉。

translations.literal: At that time all under heaven was famine-stricken; registered households relied on this to be saved.
translations.idiomatic: In a time of famine that windfall kept countless families alive.

sentences.zh: 戴若思，廣陵人也，名犯高祖廟諱。

translations.literal: Dai Ruosi was a native of Guangling; his given name tabooed the high ancestor's temple name.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Ruosi came from Guangling; his personal name violated the temple taboo of the founding emperor (hence he is known by his courtesy name).

sentences.zh: 祖烈，吳左將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lie was Wu's general of the left.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dai Lie had been general of the left under Wu.

sentences.zh: 父昌，會稽太守。

translations.literal: His father Chang was Kuaiji administrator.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dai Chang was governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 若思有風儀，性閑爽，少好遊俠，不拘操行。

translations.literal: Ruosi had bearing and manner, nature leisurely and open; in youth he loved wandering knighthood, not binding conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Ruosi cut a striking figure, easygoing and bold; in youth he roamed as a knight-errant and scorned petty rules.

sentences.zh: 遇陸機赴洛，船裝甚盛，遂與其徒掠之。

translations.literal: Encountering Lu Ji going to Luoyang, the boat's outfitting was very rich; thereupon with his followers he plundered it.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Ji sailed for Luoyang with a lavishly laden boat, Dai and his band robbed him.

sentences.zh: 若思登岸，據胡床，指麾同旅，皆得其宜。

translations.literal: Ruosi ascended the bank, leaned on a folding stool, directed his companions—all obtained their proper roles.
translations.idiomatic: He stepped ashore, sat on a camp stool, and deployed his men with perfect composure.

sentences.zh: 機察見之，知非常人，在舫屋上遙謂之曰：「卿才器如此，乃復作劫邪！

translations.literal: Ji observed him, knew he was not an ordinary man; in the cabin roof he called from afar: "Your talents and capacity are thus—yet you repeat being a bandit!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji saw this was no common robber and shouted from the cabin, "With ability like yours you play the pirate?

sentences.zh: 」若思感悟，因流涕，投劍就之。

translations.literal: " Ruosi was moved to awareness, thereupon shed tears, cast aside sword and approached him.
translations.idiomatic: " Dai Ruosi broke down, wept, threw away his sword, and came forward.

sentences.zh: 機與言，深加賞異，遂與定交焉。

translations.literal: Ji spoke with him, deeply praised and marveled, thereupon with him formed friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji spoke with him, admired him deeply, and they became friends.

sentences.zh: 若思後舉孝廉，入洛，機薦之于趙王倫曰：「蓋聞繁弱登禦，然後高墉之功顯；

translations.literal: Ruosi later was recommended filial and incorrupt, entered Luoyang; Ji recommended him to Prince Zhao Lun, saying: "I have heard that when Fanruo mounts the chariot, then the high wall's achievement appears;
translations.idiomatic: Later, recommended as filial and incorrupt, Dai Ruosi went to Luoyang; Lu Ji commended him to Sima Lun: "When the great bow is strung, high walls fall;

sentences.zh: 孤竹在肆，然後降神之曲成。

translations.literal: when Guzhu is in the shop, then the spirit-descending tune is completed.
translations.idiomatic: when Guzhu bamboo is offered in the market, the gods' music can be made.

sentences.zh: 是以高世之主必假遠邇之器，蘊櫝之才思托太音之和。

translations.literal: Therefore rulers who transcend the age must borrow instruments from far and near; talents hidden in boxes think to entrust themselves to the great harmony's tone.
translations.idiomatic: Thus a true king borrows talent from every quarter; gems still wrapped in cloth long for a place in the royal orchestra.

sentences.zh: 伏見處士廣陵戴若思，年三十，清沖履道，德量允塞；

translations.literal: Your servant sees recluse Guangling Dai Ruosi, age thirty, pure and calm treading the Way, virtue and capacity truly filling;
translations.idiomatic: I present the recluse Dai Ruosi of Guangling, thirty years old, serene in virtue and ample in character;

sentences.zh: 思理足以研幽，才鑒足以辯物；

translations.literal: thought and pattern suffice to probe the subtle; talent and mirror suffice to distinguish things;
translations.idiomatic: his mind plumbs the subtle, his judgment sorts true from false;

sentences.zh: 安窮樂志，無風塵之慕，砥節立行，有井渫之潔；

translations.literal: content in poverty, joyful in aspiration, without wind and dust's longing; grinding integrity, establishing conduct, having the well-rope's purity;
translations.idiomatic: he loves poverty and clear purpose, never hankers after vulgar rank, and keeps a well-rope's unstained honor;

sentences.zh: 誠東南之遺寶，宰朝之奇璞也。

translations.literal: truly the southeast's leftover treasure, the court's marvelous uncut jade.
translations.idiomatic: he is the southeast's hidden treasure, the court's unpolished jade.

sentences.zh: 若得托跡康衢，則能結軌驥騄；

translations.literal: If he can entrust his tracks to the great thoroughfare, then he can join traces with Ji and Lu;
translations.idiomatic: Set him on the high road and he will keep pace with the finest steeds;

sentences.zh: 曜質廊廟，必能垂光璵璠矣。

translations.literal: if his substance is displayed in the corridor temple, he will surely be able to hang light on fine jade.
translations.idiomatic: bring him to the hall and his radiance will adorn the regalia.

sentences.zh: 惟明公垂神采察，不使忠允之言以人而廢。

translations.literal: Only may the enlightened duke let fall spiritual glance and examine, not let loyal and fitting words be abandoned because of the person.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to look past rumor and not dismiss honest counsel for personal reasons.

sentences.zh: 」倫乃辟之，除沁水令，不就，遂往武陵省父。

translations.literal: " Lun thereupon summoned him, appointed Qinshui magistrate; he did not take office, then went to Wuling to visit his father.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Lun appointed him magistrate of Qinshui; he declined and went to Wuling to see his father.

sentences.zh: 時同郡人潘京素有理鑒，名知人，其父遣若思就京與語，既而稱若思有公輔之才。

translations.literal: At that time fellow townsman Pan Jing by nature had pattern mirror, was famed for knowing men; his father sent Ruosi to Jing to converse; afterward Jing declared Ruosi had ministerial talent.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jing of the same commandery was famed as a judge of character; Dai's father sent the young man to meet him, and Pan pronounced him fit for the highest office.

sentences.zh: 累轉東海王越軍諮祭酒，出補豫章太守，加振威將軍，領義軍都督。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Prince Donghai Yue's army deliberation libationer, went out to fill Yuzhang administrator, added general who rouses might, concurrently righteous army area commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to deliberation libationer on Sima Yue's staff, then became governor of Yuzhang with the title general who rouses might and commander of volunteer forces.

sentences.zh: 以討賊有功，賜爵秣陵侯，遷治書侍御史、驃騎司馬，拜散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Because punishing bandits had merit, was granted noble rank Moling marquis, transferred document drafting attendant censor, chief clerk to the commander-in-chief, appointed cavalier gentleman attendant.
translations.idiomatic: For suppressing rebels he was enfeoffed as marquis of Moling, promoted to drafting censor, chief clerk to the commander-in-chief, and cavalier gentleman attendant.

sentences.zh: 元帝召為鎮東右司馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan summoned him as general who garrisons the east's right chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan named him senior clerk to the general who garrisons the east.

sentences.zh: 將征杜弢，加若思前將軍，未發而弢滅。

translations.literal: He was to campaign against Du Tao, added Ruosi as general of the van; before setting out Tao was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Tao was to be attacked, Dai Ruosi was named general of the van, but Du Tao fell before he marched.

sentences.zh: 帝為晉王，以為尚書。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Jin, he made him Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan held the title Prince of Jin, Dai Ruosi joined the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中興建，為中護軍，轉護軍將軍、尚書僕射，皆辭不拜。

translations.literal: When the restoration was founded, he became central guards commander, transferred general of the guards army, vice director of the secretariat—all declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the eastern court he was offered central guards commander, then general of the guards army and vice director of the secretariat, and each time declined.

sentences.zh: 出為征西將軍、都督兗豫幽冀雍並六州諸軍事、假節，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He went out as general who campaigns west, area commander for military affairs of Yan, Yu, You, Ji, Yong, and Bing six provinces, with credential, added cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He then took the field as general who campaigns west with command over six provinces, imperial credentials, and the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 發投刺王官千人為軍吏，調揚州百姓家奴萬人為兵配之，以散騎常侍王遐為軍司，鎮壽陽，與劉隗同出。

translations.literal: He dispatched a thousand officials who had presented calling cards to become army clerks, levied ten thousand household slaves of Yangzhou commoners as soldiers assigned to them, made cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Wang Xia army director, garrisoned Shouyang, and set out together with Liu Kui.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a thousand nominal officials as staff, impressed ten thousand Yangzhou bond servants as troops, named Wang Xia army director, and marched to Shouyang beside Liu Kui.

sentences.zh: 帝親幸其營，勞勉將士，臨發祖餞，置酒賦詩。

translations.literal: The emperor personally visited his camp, encouraged the officers and soldiers; on the eve of departure held a farewell feast, set out wine and composed poems.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited his camp in person, feasted the army on the eve of departure, and joined them in verse.

sentences.zh: 若思至合肥，而王敦舉兵，詔追若思還鎮京都，進驃騎將軍，與右衛將軍郭逸夾道築壘於大桁之北。

translations.literal: When Ruosi reached Hefei, Wang Dun raised troops; an edict recalled Ruosi to garrison the capital region, promoted general of swift cavalry, with General of the Right Guard Guo Yi built ramparts along both sides of the road north of the great floating bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Near Hefei word came that Wang Dun had risen; Dai Ruosi was recalled to defend the capital as general of swift cavalry and, with Guo Yi of the right guard, threw up earthworks north of the great bridge.

sentences.zh: 尋而石頭失守，若思與諸軍攻石頭，王師敗績。

translations.literal: Soon Stone Citadel fell; Ruosi with the various armies attacked Stone Citadel; the royal army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Stone Citadel soon fell; Dai Ruosi led the assault and the imperial forces broke.

sentences.zh: 若思率麾下百餘人赴宮受詔，與公卿百官於石頭見敦。

translations.literal: Ruosi led more than a hundred men under his command to hurry to the palace to receive edict, with dukes and ministers and hundred officials met Dun at Stone Citadel.
translations.idiomatic: He took a hundred followers to the palace for orders, then joined the high ministers to face Wang Dun at Stone Citadel.

sentences.zh: 敦問若思曰：「前日之戰有餘力乎？

translations.literal: Dun asked Ruosi: "In the battle the other day was there surplus strength?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun asked, "Did you hold anything back in the last fight?

sentences.zh: 」若思不謝而答曰：「豈敢有餘，但力不足耳。

translations.literal: " Ruosi did not apologize but answered: "How dare there be surplus—only strength was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: " Dai Ruosi answered coolly, "I had no strength left to hide—only too little, not too much.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「吾此舉動，天下以為如何？

translations.literal: " Again said: "My this movement—what does all under heaven think of it?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Dun pressed, "What does the realm make of my action?

sentences.zh: 」若思曰：「見形者謂之逆，體誠者謂之忠。

translations.literal: " Ruosi said: "Those who see the form call it rebellion; those who grasp the substance call it loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: " Dai Ruosi said, "Surface judgment calls it treason; those who see the heart may call it loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」敦笑曰：「卿可謂能言。

translations.literal: " Dun laughed and said: "You may be called able to speak.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Dun laughed, "You are eloquent, I grant you.

sentences.zh: 」敦參軍呂猗昔為台郎，有刀筆才，性尤奸諂，若思為尚書，惡其為人，猗亦深憾焉。

translations.literal: " Dun's military adviser Lu Yi formerly was a terrace gentleman, had knife-brush talent, nature especially treacherous and fawning; when Ruosi was Masters of Writing, he hated his person; Yi also deeply resented.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi, Wang Dun's adviser, had been a petty clerk, facile with documents, and a sycophant; Dai Ruosi had despised him at the secretariat, and Lu Yi hated him in return.

sentences.zh: 至是，乃說敦曰：「周顗、戴若思皆有高名，足以惑眾，近者之言曾無愧色。

translations.literal: At this point, he persuaded Dun: "Zhou Yi and Dai Ruosi both have high fame, sufficient to delude the multitude; their recent words showed not the least shame.
translations.idiomatic: Now Lu Yi urged Wang Dun, "Zhou Yi and Dai Ruosi command such prestige that they sway the crowd, yet they answered you without a blush.

sentences.zh: 公若不除，恐有再舉之患，為將來之憂耳。

translations.literal: If the duke does not eliminate them, I fear there will be the disaster of a second rising, becoming worry for the future.
translations.idiomatic: If you spare them they will stir a second revolt—that is the danger ahead.

sentences.zh: 」敦以為然，又素忌之，俄而遣鄧岳、繆坦收若思而害之。

translations.literal: " Dun thought it right, and by nature already envied them; soon sent Deng Yue and Miu Tan to seize Ruosi and harm him.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Dun agreed; he already envied both men and soon sent Deng Yue and Miu Tan to arrest Dai Ruosi and kill him.

sentences.zh: 若思素有重望，四海之士莫不痛惜焉。

translations.literal: Ruosi by nature had heavy reputation; gentlemen of the four seas none did not painfully regret him.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Ruosi had enjoyed immense prestige, and men across the realm mourned his death.

sentences.zh: 賊平，冊贈右光祿大夫、儀同三司，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was posthumously enfeoffed as right household grandee, peerage equal to the Three Offices, posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion he was canonized as right household grandee with Three Dukes parity and the posthumous name "Jian" (Sparing).

sentences.zh: 邈字望之。

translations.literal: Miao's courtesy name was Wangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Miao, courtesy name Wangzhi.

sentences.zh: 少好學，尤精《史》《漢》，才不逮若思，儒博過之。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, especially mastered the "Histories" and "Han"; talent did not match Ruosi, in Confucian breadth he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books from boyhood, above all the Records and the Han history; he lacked Dai Ruosi's flash but surpassed him in scholarly breadth.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉秀才，尋遷太子洗馬，出補西陽內史。

translations.literal: At capping he was recommended cultivated talent, soon transferred crown prince's groom, went out to fill Xiyang interior secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination at twenty, became crown prince's groom, then governor of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，元帝版行邵陵內史、丞相軍諮祭酒，出為征南軍司。

translations.literal: In Yongjia, Emperor Yuan by emergency appointment made him acting Shaoling interior secretary, chief minister's army deliberation libationer, went out as south expedition army director.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongjia, Emperor Yuan named him acting governor of Shaoling, deliberation libationer on the chief minister's staff, then army director on the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 于時凡百草創，學校未立，邈上疏曰：

translations.literal: At that time everything was first establishment, schools were not yet set up; Miao submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The empire was still being built and no schools existed; Dai Miao presented a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天道之所大，莫大於陰陽；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in what the way of heaven makes great, nothing is greater than yin and yang;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's greatest workings are yin and yang;

sentences.zh: 帝王之至務，莫重於禮學。

translations.literal: in emperors' utmost tasks, nothing is weightier than ritual learning.
translations.idiomatic: a monarch's first duty is ritual and education.

sentences.zh: 是以古之建國，有明堂辟雍之制，鄉有庠序1111校之儀，皆所以抽導幽滯，啟廣才思。

translations.literal: Therefore in antiquity in establishing the state there was bright hall and royal academy system; in villages there was the pattern of village schools, order schools, and academies—all used to draw forth the hidden and blocked, open and broaden talent and thought.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients founded the capital with a bright hall and a royal academy, and every district had its village schools—all to draw talent from obscurity and sharpen minds.

sentences.zh: 蓋以六四有困蒙之吝，君子大養正之功也。

translations.literal: In general because the hexagrams speak of ignorant youth's shame, the nobleman esteems the work of great nurturing of the upright.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes warn against leaving the young in darkness; the gentleman therefore cultivates rectitude above all.

sentences.zh: 昔仲尼列國之大夫耳，興禮修學於洙泗之間，四方髦俊斐然向風，身達者七十餘人。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhongni was merely a great officer among the states; he raised ritual and cultivated learning between Zhu and Si; four corners' handsome talents flourished and turned to the wind; those who personally succeeded were more than seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius was only a wandering minister, yet between the Zhu and Si rivers he taught ritual and learning until more than seventy disciples rose to office.

sentences.zh: 自茲以來，千載絕塵。

translations.literal: From this onward, a thousand years cut off the dust.
translations.idiomatic: For a millennium afterward that light went out.

sentences.zh: 豈天下小於魯衛，賢哲乏于曩時？

translations.literal: How could all under heaven be smaller than Lu and Wei, wise men fewer than in former times?
translations.idiomatic: Was the empire smaller than Lu or Wei? Were there fewer sages than in his day?

sentences.zh: 勵與不勵故也。

translations.literal: It is encouragement and lack of encouragement that is the cause.
translations.idiomatic: The difference lay in whether rulers bothered to encourage learning.

sentences.zh: 自頃國遭無妄之禍，社稷有綴旒之危，寇羯飲馬于長江，凶狡鴟張於萬里，遂使神州蕭條，鞠為茂草，四海之內，人跡不交。

translations.literal: Since recently the state has suffered undeserved calamity, altars of soil and grain have the danger of hanging tassels; bandit Jie watered horses at the Yangzi, vicious cunning owls spread at ten thousand li; thereupon caused divine continent desolate, rolled into thick grass; within the four seas, human tracks do not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the realm has suffered disaster, the throne has hung by a thread, barbarians have watered horses at the Yangzi, and traitors have swaggered across the map until the heartland is wasteland and travelers dare not cross the roads.

sentences.zh: 霸主有旰食之憂，黎元懷荼毒之苦，戎首交拜于中原，何遽籩豆之事哉！

translations.literal: The hegemon has worry of eating at dusk; common folk harbor bitter poison's suffering; war leaders bow to one another in the central plain—how suddenly matters of baskets and beans!
translations.idiomatic: Our leaders skip meals from worry, the people choke on misery, and warlords scrape and bow in the Yellow River plain—who has leisure for ritual vessels?

sentences.zh: 然三年不為禮，禮必壞；

translations.literal: Yet three years without performing ritual, ritual must decay;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Confucius warned: three years without ritual and the rites rot;

sentences.zh: 三年不為樂，樂必崩，況曠戴累紀如此之久邪！

translations.literal: three years without performing music, music must collapse—how much more for ages piled empty for so long!
translations.idiomatic: three years without music and harmony collapses—how much worse after generations of neglect!

sentences.zh: 今末進後生目不睹揖讓升降之儀，耳不聞鐘鼓管弦之音，文章散滅，圖讖無遺，此蓋聖達之所深悼，有識之所嗟歎也。

translations.literal: Now young men of later advancement never see with eyes the ceremonies of bowing and yielding, ascending and descending; never hear with ears bell-drum string-pipe sounds; writings scatter and perish, charts and prophecies leave no trace—this is what sages and the enlightened deeply mourn, what the knowing sigh over.
translations.idiomatic: Today's youths have never seen a proper court ceremony, never heard ritual music; texts and omens are lost—this is what every thoughtful man laments.

sentences.zh: 夫平世尚文，遭亂尚武，文武遞用，長久之道，譬之天地昏明之迭，自古以來未有不由之者也。

translations.literal: As for peaceful age esteeming culture, encountering chaos esteeming martial—culture and martial alternate in use; that is the long-lasting way; compare it to heaven and earth's dark and bright succeeding—since antiquity there has never been one who did not proceed by this.
translations.idiomatic: Peace exalts letters, turmoil exalts arms; the two must alternate like day and night—no dynasty has ever done otherwise.

sentences.zh: 今或以天下未一，非興禮學之時，此言似之而不其然。

translations.literal: Now some think because all under heaven is not yet one, it is not the time to raise ritual learning—this speech seems so yet is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the realm is still divided and schools can wait—that sounds plausible but is wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫儒道深奧，不可倉卒而成。

translations.literal: As for Confucian learning being deep and subtle, it cannot be completed in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian learning is deep; it cannot be rushed.

sentences.zh: 古之俊乂必三年而通一經，比天下平泰然後修之，則功成事定，誰與制禮作樂者哉？

translations.literal: In antiquity outstanding men necessarily took three years to master one classic; if one waits until all under heaven is level and calm and then cultivates it, then achievement is settled and affairs fixed—who will be left to regulate ritual and make music?
translations.idiomatic: Ancient scholars needed three years per classic; if we wait for perfect peace before teaching, who will be left to write the rituals and music?

sentences.zh: 又貴遊之子未必有斬將搴旗之才，亦未有從軍征戍之役，不及盛年講肄道義，使明珠加磨瑩之功，荊璞發采琢之榮，不亦良可惜乎！

translations.literal: Moreover sons of noble wandering are not necessarily those with beheading generals and seizing banners' talent; also they have not had following army campaign and garrison service—if before prime years they do not lecture and practice the Way, causing bright pearls to add grinding and polishing's work, Jing jade to issue carving and cutting's glory—is it not truly pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Scions of great houses are not all born warriors; most never see a campaign. To waste their best years without teaching the Way is to leave jade unpolished—what a loss!

sentences.zh: 臣愚以世喪道久，人情玩于所習；

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks the age has long lost the Way, human feelings play on what they are used to;
translations.idiomatic: I fear men have grown used to moral chaos;

sentences.zh: 純風日去，華競日彰，猶火之消膏而莫之覺也。

translations.literal: pure wind daily departs, flashy rivalry daily shines forth, like fire consuming fat yet none perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: decency ebbs while vanity rises, like fat melting in a fire unseen.

sentences.zh: 今天地告始，萬物權輿，聖朝以神武之德，值革命之運，蕩近世之流弊，繼千載之絕軌，篤道崇儒，創立大業。

translations.literal: Now heaven and earth announce the beginning, myriad things are in first growth; the sage court by divine martial virtue meets the revolution's turn, sweeps away recent age's flowing ills, continues a thousand years' severed track, honors the Way and esteems Confucians, founds the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth have turned a new page; this court, with martial vigor and a mandate to renew the age, sweeps away late Jin decay and revives learning.

sentences.zh: 明主唱之於上，宰輔督之於下。

translations.literal: The enlightened ruler initiates it above, chief ministers supervise it below.
translations.idiomatic: Let the sovereign champion it above and the ministers enforce it below.

sentences.zh: 夫上之所好，下必有過之者焉，是故雙劍之節崇，而飛白之俗成；

translations.literal: As for what those above love, those below surely have those who exceed it; therefore when twin-sword ceremony is honored, flying-white custom forms;
translations.idiomatic: The people ape their betters: honor swordsmanship and bravado spreads;

sentences.zh: 挾琴之容飾，而赴曲之和作；

translations.literal: when hugging-lute bearing is adorned, then tunes that catch the melody arise;
translations.idiomatic: praise lute-bearing dandies and shallow music thrives;

sentences.zh: 君子之德風，小人之德草，實在感之而已。

translations.literal: the nobleman's virtue is wind, the petty man's virtue is grass—it truly lies in what moves them.
translations.idiomatic: the gentleman is wind, the commoner grass—example is everything.

sentences.zh: 臣以暗淺，不能遠識格言；

translations.literal: Your servant, being dim and shallow, cannot from afar recognize model sayings;
translations.idiomatic: I am too dull to add lofty doctrine;

sentences.zh: 奉誦明令，慷慨下風，謂宜以三時之隙漸就修建。

translations.literal: reverently chanting the enlightened order, stirred below the wind, say it is fitting in the three seasons' gaps gradually to proceed with construction.
translations.idiomatic: but reading your edict I urge that we use slack seasons to rebuild schools step by step.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，納焉，於是始修禮學。

translations.literal: The memorial was presented and accepted; from this they began to cultivate ritual learning.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved, and the court began to restore ritual education.

sentences.zh: 代劉隗為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He replaced Liu Kui as Danyang intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Liu Kui as governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 王敦作逆，加左將軍。

translations.literal: Wang Dun raised rebellion; Miao was added general of the left.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled, Dai Miao was named general of the left.

sentences.zh: 及敦得志，而若思遇害，邈坐免官。

translations.literal: When Dun obtained his will, yet Ruosi met harm, Miao sat guilty and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun triumphed and Dai Ruosi was killed, Dai Miao lost his post as an accomplice.

sentences.zh: 敦誅後，拜尚書僕射。

translations.literal: After Dun was executed, Miao was appointed vice director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun fell, Dai Miao became vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈衛將軍，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: He died in office, posthumously gifted general who guards the army, posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office, canonized as general who guards the army with the posthumous name "Mu" (Solemn).

sentences.zh: 子謐嗣，曆義興太守、大司農。

translations.literal: His son Mi inherited; he passed through Yixing administrator, minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dai Mi succeeded him, serving as governor of Yixing and minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 周顗，字伯仁，安東將軍浚之子也。

translations.literal: Zhou Yi, courtesy name Boren, was the son of general who garrisons the east Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi, courtesy name Boren, was the son of Zhou Jun, general who garrisons the east.

sentences.zh: 少有重名，神彩秀徹，雖時輩親狎，莫能媟也。

translations.literal: In youth he had heavy fame, spirit and radiance clear through; though contemporaries were intimate, none could treat him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he was famed for luminous dignity; friends might jest with him, but none took him lightly.

sentences.zh: 司徒掾同郡賁嵩有清操，見顗，歎曰：「汝潁固多奇士！

translations.literal: Steward's aide fellow townsman Ben Song had pure conduct; seeing Yi, he sighed, saying: "Your Ying region indeed has many strange knights!
translations.idiomatic: Ben Song, a steward's aide from the same commandery, was a man of integrity; meeting Zhou Yi he exclaimed, "Yingchuan still breeds marvels!

sentences.zh: 自頃雅道陵遲，今復見周伯仁，將振起舊風，清我邦族矣。

translations.literal: Since recently the elegant way has declined; now again seeing Zhou Boren, he will rouse the old wind and purify our clan and lineage.
translations.idiomatic: The old refinement has faded, yet here is Zhou Boren to revive it for our people.

sentences.zh: 」廣陵戴若思東南之美，舉秀才，入洛，素聞顗名，往候之，終坐而出，不敢顯其才辯。

translations.literal: " Guangling Dai Ruosi was the southeast's finest; recommended cultivated talent, entered Luoyang; by nature had heard Yi's fame, went to visit him; sat through the whole meeting and departed, dared not display his talent and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: " Dai Ruosi of Guangling, the southeast's leading talent, went to Luoyang on recommendation and called on Zhou Yi; he sat silent through the visit, too awed to show off his wit.

sentences.zh: 顗從弟穆亦有美譽，欲陵折顗，顗陶然弗與之校，於是人士益宗附之。

translations.literal: Yi's cousin Mu also had fine reputation, wished to overwhelm and break Yi; Yi was expansively pleased and did not contend with him; thereupon gentlemen all the more gathered to attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Zhou Mu tried to upstage him, but Zhou Yi only smiled and refused the contest—so the elite flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 州郡辟命皆不就。

translations.literal: Provincial and commandery summonses he all did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He turned down every provincial appointment.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，襲父爵武城侯，拜秘書郎，累遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: At capping, he inherited his father's noble rank Wucheng marquis, was appointed secretary gentleman, gradually transferred Masters of Writing personnel gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he inherited the Wucheng marquisate, joined the palace library, and rose to personnel director at the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 東海王越子毗為鎮軍將軍，以顗為長史。

translations.literal: Prince Donghai Yue's son Pi was general who garrisons the army; he made Yi chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Pi, son of Sima Yue, named him chief clerk when Pi held the post of general who garrisons the army.

sentences.zh: 元帝初鎮江左，請為軍諮祭酒，出為甯遠將軍、荊州刺史、領護南蠻校尉、假節。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan first garrisoned the Yangzi left, he requested Yi as army deliberation libationer, went out as general who brings peace from afar, Jing province inspector, concurrently colonel who guards the southern barbarians, with credential.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan first held the lower Yangzi, he made Zhou Yi deliberation libationer, then inspector of Jing with the southern-barbarian command and imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 始到州，而建平流人傅密等叛迎蜀賊杜弢，顗狼狽失據。

translations.literal: He had just reached the province when Jianping wandering people Fu Mi and others rebelled and welcomed Shu bandit Du Tao; Yi was in dire straits and lost footing.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely arrived when refugees at Jianping rose under Fu Mi for Du Tao and left him stranded.

sentences.zh: 陶侃遣將吳寄以兵救之，故顗得免，因奔王敦于豫章。

translations.literal: Tao Kan sent general Wu Ji with troops to rescue him; therefore Yi was able to escape, then fled to Wang Dun at Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan's officer Wu Ji relieved him, so Zhou Yi escaped to Wang Dun in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 敦留之。

translations.literal: Dun kept him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun kept him at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 軍司戴邈曰：「顗雖退敗，未有蒞眾之咎，德望素重，宜還復之。

translations.literal: Army director Dai Miao said: "Although Yi retreated in defeat, he has not the fault of presiding over the masses; virtue and reputation have long been heavy—it is fitting to return and restore him.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Miao urged, "Zhou Yi lost a battle but never betrayed his command; his prestige is intact—send him back.

sentences.zh: 」敦不從。

translations.literal: Dun did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun refused.

sentences.zh: 帝召為揚威將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him as general who displays might, Yan province inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named him general who displays might and inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 顗還建康，帝留顗不遣，復以為軍諮祭酒，尋轉右長史。

translations.literal: Yi returned to Jiankang; the emperor kept Yi and did not dispatch him, again made him army deliberation libationer, soon transferred right chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yi reached Jiankang, the emperor kept him at court as deliberation libationer, then senior clerk on the right.

sentences.zh: 中興建，補吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the restoration was founded, he was appointed minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the eastern Jin he became minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以醉酒為有司所糾，白衣領職。

translations.literal: Shortly, because of drunk wine he was impeached by the responsible office; in white garments he held the post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a drinking bout brought a censor's charge; he kept his duties while demoted to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 復坐門生斫傷人，免官。

translations.literal: Again he sat guilty because a household retainer hacked and wounded a person; dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When a client of his household wounded someone, he was stripped of office again.

sentences.zh: 太興初，更拜太子少傅，尚書如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixing, he was again appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent, Masters of Writing as before.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taixing he was named junior tutor to the crown prince while keeping his secretariat post.

sentences.zh: 顗上疏讓曰：「臣退自循省，學不通一經，智不效一官，止足良難，未能守分，遂忝顯任，名位過量。

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial declining, saying: "Your servant retiring examines himself: learning does not penetrate one classic, wisdom does not effect one office; to stop and be content is truly hard; unable to guard my portion, I have rashly assumed eminent office—name and position exceed measure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi begged off: "I have mastered no single classic and proved myself in no single post; I cannot stay within my limits, yet I hold high rank—far beyond my weight.

sentences.zh: 不悟天鑒忘臣頑弊，乃欲使臣內管銓衡，外忝傅訓，質輕蟬翼，事重千鈞，此之不可，不待識而明矣。

translations.literal: I did not realize heaven's mirror would forget your servant's stubborn decay, yet wish to make your servant within manage personnel scales, without disgrace tutor's instruction—substance lighter than cicada wings, affairs heavier than thousand jun—this cannot be, it does not await knowledge to be clear.
translations.idiomatic: Now you would have me judge men within and teach the heir without—my talent is lighter than a cicada's wing, the burden heavier than a thousand stone weights; the mismatch is obvious.

sentences.zh: 若臣受負乘之責，必貽聖朝惟塵之恥，俯仰愧懼，不知所圖。

translations.literal: If your servant receives the blame of riding when unfit, it will surely leave the sage court the shame of dust-only teams; bowing and rising I am ashamed and fearful, not knowing what to plan.
translations.idiomatic: If I accept and fail, I will disgrace the court; I am terrified and see no way forward.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「紹幼沖便居儲副之貴，當賴軌匠以祛蒙蔽。

translations.literal: " The edict said: "Shao is young and already dwells in the heir apparent's nobility; he ought to rely on the model craftsman to dispel blindness.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "The crown prince is young; he needs a model to clear his mind.

sentences.zh: 望之儼然，斯不言之益，何學之習邪，所謂與田蘇遊忘其鄙心者。

translations.literal: Wangzhi's dignified bearing is the benefit of not speaking—what need to study? This is what is called roaming with Tian Su and forgetting vulgar mind.
translations.idiomatic: Your dignified presence teaches without lessons—like the ancients who forgot low desires in good company.

sentences.zh: 便當副往意，不宜沖讓。

translations.literal: You ought to accord with former intent; it is not fitting to decline modestly.
translations.idiomatic: Accept the post; do not refuse.

sentences.zh: 」轉尚書左僕射，領吏部如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred left vice director of the secretariat, concurrently minister of personnel as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left vice director of the secretariat while remaining minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 庾亮嘗謂顗曰：「諸人咸以君方樂廣。

translations.literal: Yu Liang once said to Yi: "The host of men all compare you to Yue Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang told him, "Everyone likens you to Yue Guang.

sentences.zh: 」顗曰：「何乃刻畫無鹽，唐突西施也。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "How is that carving Wuyan and offending Xishi!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Yi answered, "That is like painting Wuyan the ugly and calling her Xi Shi.

sentences.zh: 」帝宴群公於西堂，酒酣，從容曰：「今日名臣共集，何如堯舜時邪？

translations.literal: " The emperor feasted the host of dukes in the west hall; wine deep, calmly said: "Today famous ministers gather together—how does it compare to Yao and Shun's age?
translations.idiomatic: At a western-hall banquet the emperor asked tipsily how his court compared to Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 」顗因醉厲聲曰：「今雖同人主，何得復比聖世！

translations.literal: " Yi because drunk spoke sharply: "Now although we share a lord, how can we again compare to a sage age!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Yi, drunk, snapped, "We may share a throne, but we are no sage-kings!

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒而起，手詔付廷尉，將加戮，累日方赦之。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly angry and rose, hand edict delivered to the commandant of justice, was about to add execution; after accumulated days then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor nearly had him executed, then relented after several days.

sentences.zh: 及出，諸公就省，顗曰：「近日之罪，固知不至於死。

translations.literal: When he came out, the host of dukes came to console; Yi said: "The recent crime, I firmly knew would not reach death.
translations.idiomatic: When friends visited him in disgrace, he said, "I knew I would not die for that.

sentences.zh: 」尋代戴若思為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Dai Ruosi as general of the guards army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he succeeded Dai Ruosi as general of the guards army.

sentences.zh: 尚書紀瞻置酒請顗及王導等，顗荒醉失儀，復為有司所奏。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing Ji Zhan set wine and invited Yi and Wang Dao and others; Yi wildly drunk lost deportment, again was memorialized by the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan hosted Zhou Yi and Wang Dao; Zhou Yi drank himself into another scandal.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「顗參副朝右，職掌銓衡，當敬慎德音，式是百辟。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Yi participates as deputy at court's right, office holds personnel scales; he ought to revere and be cautious in virtue's voice, model himself to the hundred shepherds.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked him: "As vice director and minister of personnel you must exemplify decorum for every official.

sentences.zh: 屢以酒過，為有司所繩。

translations.literal: Repeatedly because of wine faults, he has been bound by the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: Wine has brought you before the censors again and again.

sentences.zh: 吾亮其極歎之情，然亦是濡首之誡也。

translations.literal: I understand his utmost sighing feeling, yet this also is the warning of drenched head.
translations.idiomatic: I grant your passions run deep, but this is also the warning of the sodden head.

sentences.zh: 顗必能克己復禮者，今不加黜責。」

translations.literal: If Yi surely can restrain himself and return to ritual, now we do not add dismissal and blame."
translations.idiomatic: If you can master yourself, we will not dismiss you."

sentences.zh: 初，顗以雅望獲海內盛名，後頗以酒失。

translations.literal: At first Yi by elegant reputation obtained sea-within great fame; afterward he quite because of wine lost control.
translations.idiomatic: Once famed for dignity, he later ruined himself with drink.

sentences.zh: 為僕射，略無醒日，時人號為「三日僕射」。

translations.literal: As vice director, there was almost no sober day; people of the time called him "three-day vice director."
translations.idiomatic: As vice director he was seldom sober; men called him the "three-day vice director."

sentences.zh: 庾亮曰：「周侯末年，所謂鳳德之衰也。

translations.literal: Yu Liang said: "Marquis Zhou in his final years—what is called the phoenix virtue's decline.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang said, "Zhou Yi in his last years showed the waning of phoenix virtue.

sentences.zh: 」顗在中朝時，能飲酒一石，及過江，雖日醉，每稱無對。

translations.literal: " When Yi was in the central court, he could drink one dan of wine; after crossing the Yangzi, though daily drunk, each time declared he had no match.
translations.idiomatic: " In Luoyang he could down a full dan; south of the river he boasted while drunk that no one could match his cup.

sentences.zh: 偶有舊對從北來，顗遇之欣然，乃出酒二石共飲，各大醉。

translations.literal: Occasionally an old drinking partner came from the north; Yi met him joyfully, then brought out two dan of wine to drink together; both greatly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: When an old drinking friend arrived from the north, Zhou Yi hauled out two dan and they drank themselves under.

sentences.zh: 及顗醒，使視客，已腐脅而死。

translations.literal: When Yi awoke, he sent to look at the guest—already rotten in the ribs and dead.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yi woke, his guest had died of drink.

sentences.zh: 顗性寬裕而友愛過人，弟嵩嘗因酒嗔目謂顗曰：「君才不及弟，何乃橫得重名！

translations.literal: Yi's nature was generous and tolerant, yet friendship surpassed others; younger brother Song once because of wine glared and said to Yi: "Your talent does not match younger brother's—how do you rashly obtain heavy reputation!
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhou Song once snarled drunk, "You are less able than I—how dare you outrank me in fame?

sentences.zh: 」以所燃蠟燭投之。

translations.literal: " He cast at him the candle he was burning.
translations.idiomatic: He threw the burning candle at him.

sentences.zh: 顗神色無忤，徐曰：「阿奴火攻，固出下策耳。

translations.literal: Yi's spirit and bearing showed no offense; slowly said: "Little brother's fire attack—indeed is lower strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi only said calmly, "Brother, fire attacks are a low tactic.

sentences.zh: 」王導甚重之，嘗枕顗膝而指其腹曰：「此中何所有也？

translations.literal: " Wang Dao greatly esteemed him; once pillowed on Yi's knee and pointed at his belly, saying: "What is inside here?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Dao admired him, once rested on his knee and asked what lay in his belly.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「此中空洞無物，然足容卿輩數百人。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Inside here is empty without things, yet sufficient to hold you lot several hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Yi said, "Nothing at all—yet room enough for hundreds like you.

sentences.zh: 」導亦不以為忤。

translations.literal: " Dao also did not take it as offense.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Dao laughed it off.

sentences.zh: 又于導坐傲然嘯詠，導云：「卿欲希嵇、阮邪？

translations.literal: Again at Dao's seat he proudly whistled and chanted; Dao said: "Do you wish to emulate Ji and Ruan?
translations.idiomatic: Once he whistled loudly at Wang Dao's party; Wang Dao asked if he meant to imitate Ji Kang and Ruan Ji.

sentences.zh: 」顗曰：「何敢近舍明公，遠希嵇、阮。」

translations.literal: " Yi said: "How dare I near abandon the enlightened duke and far emulate Ji and Ruan."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Yi replied, "I would not neglect my host to mimic long-dead eccentrics."

sentences.zh: 及王敦構逆，溫嶠謂顗曰：「大將軍此舉似有所在，當無濫邪？

translations.literal: When Wang Dun framed rebellion, Wen Qiao said to Yi: "The grand general this movement seems to have a target—surely it is not indiscriminate?
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rose, Wen Qiao asked Zhou Yi if the coup had a limited aim.

sentences.zh: 」顗曰：「君少年未更事。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "You are young and have not experienced affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Yi answered, "You are young and inexperienced.

sentences.zh: 人主自非堯舜，何能無失，人臣豈可得舉兵以協主！

translations.literal: The lord by nature unless Yao and Shun—how can there be no fault? How can subjects obtain raising troops to coerce the ruler!
translations.idiomatic: No ruler is flawless as Yao or Shun; still, no minister may raise arms to bully his sovereign!

sentences.zh: 共相推戴，未能數年，一旦如此，豈云非亂乎！

translations.literal: Mutually we have supported and honored—unable to count years—suddenly like this—how can one say it is not chaos!
translations.idiomatic: We have hailed this throne only a few years—how is this not treason?

sentences.zh: 處仲剛愎強忍，狼抗無上，其意寧有限邪！

translations.literal: Chuzhong is stubborn and forceful, cruel and resistant without respect above—his intent how can it have limit!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun is ruthless, defiant, and respects no one above him—his ambition knows no bound!

sentences.zh: 」既而王師敗績，顗奉詔詣敦，敦曰：「伯仁，卿負我！

translations.literal: " Soon the royal army was defeated; Yi received edict and went to Dun; Dun said: "Boren, you have failed me!
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army broke, Zhou Yi was sent to Wang Dun, who accused him: "Boren, you betrayed me!

sentences.zh: 」顗曰：「公戎車犯順，下官親率六軍，不能其事，使王旅奔敗，以此負公。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "Your lordship's war chariot violated obedience; your inferior personally led the six armies yet could not accomplish the affair, caused the royal host to flee in defeat—with this I have failed your lordship.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Yi replied, "You turned rebel; I commanded the imperial armies and failed—that is how I failed you.

sentences.zh: 」敦憚其辭正，不知所答。

translations.literal: " Dun feared his words' rectitude, did not know what to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, stung by his candor, had no reply.

sentences.zh: 帝召顗於廣室，謂之曰：「近日大事，二宮無恙，諸人平安，大將軍故副所望邪？

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Yi to the broad chamber, said to him: "Recently the great affair—both palaces unharmed, the host of men safe—is the grand general indeed as deputy to what was hoped?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took Zhou Yi aside: "The coup is over; the palaces are safe—do you think the grand general has done what we wished?

sentences.zh: 」顗曰：「二宮自如明詔，於臣等故未可知。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "The two palaces are as the enlightened edict; as for your servants, it is still not knowable.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Yi said, "The palaces are safe by your grace; as for us ministers, who can tell?

sentences.zh: 」護軍長史郝嘏等勸顗避敦，顗曰：「吾備位大臣，朝廷喪敗，寧可復草間求活，外投胡越邪！

translations.literal: " Guards army chief clerk Hao Gu and others urged Yi to avoid Dun; Yi said: "I occupy a great minister's place; the court has suffered defeat—how could I again seek life among the weeds and flee abroad to Hu or Yue!
translations.idiomatic: Friends urged him to hide from Wang Dun; he refused: "I am a high minister; I will not skulk in the grass or flee to barbarians.

sentences.zh: 」俄而與戴若思俱被收，路經太廟，顗大言曰：「天地先帝之靈；

translations.literal: " Soon he together with Dai Ruosi was both seized; passing the great temple, Yi spoke loudly: "Spirits of Heaven and the former emperors;
translations.idiomatic: Seized with Dai Ruosi and marched past the imperial shrine, he shouted, "Spirits of Heaven and our late kings!

sentences.zh: 賊臣王敦傾覆社稷，枉殺忠臣，陵虐天下，神祇有靈，當速殺敦，無令縱毒，以傾王室。

translations.literal: rebel minister Wang Dun has overturned altars of soil and grain, wrongfully slain loyal ministers, tyrannized all under heaven—if the spirits have power, swiftly kill Dun, do not let him spread poison to overturn the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: The traitor Wang Dun has ruined the state and murdered loyal men—if you have power, strike him down before he destroys the dynasty!

sentences.zh: 」語未終，收人以戟傷其口，血流至踵，顏色不變，容止自若，觀者皆為流涕。

translations.literal: " Before words ended, the arresters with halberd wounded his mouth; blood flowed to heels; color unchanged, bearing and deportment self-possessed; onlookers all for him shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Guards rammed a halberd into his mouth before he finished; blood ran to his heels, yet his face never changed, and the crowd wept.

sentences.zh: 遂于石頭南門外石上害之，時年五十四。

translations.literal: Thereupon on Stone Citadel south gate outside on stone they harmed him; at the time age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: They killed him on the stone outside Stone Citadel's south gate; he was fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 顗之死也，敦坐有一參軍樗蒱，馬於博頭被殺，因謂敦曰：「周家奕世令望，而位不至公，及伯仁將登而墜，有似下官此馬。

translations.literal: At Yi's death, Dun's seat had a military adviser playing the chupu game; a horse at the throw was killed; thereupon he said to Dun: "The Zhou house for generations has fine reputation, yet rank did not reach duke; when Boren was about to ascend yet fell—like this inferior's horse.
translations.idiomatic: During the chupu game at Wang Dun's table a piece horse was removed; a player quipped that the Zhou clan, always eminent, never reached ducal rank—like that doomed horse.

sentences.zh: 」敦曰：「伯仁總角於東宮相遇，一面披襟，便許之三事，何圖不幸自貽王法。

translations.literal: " Dun said: "Boren in childhood hair-knot met at eastern palace; one meeting opening lapels, then promised him three matters—how could I have thought misfortune would bring him into kingly law.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Dun said, "Boren and I were boys together in the heir's palace; I swore three promises—never that the law would take him.

sentences.zh: 」敦素憚顗，每見顗輒面熱，雖復冬月，扇面手不得休。

translations.literal: Dun by nature feared Yi; each time he saw Yi then face grew hot; though again winter month, fanning face hand could not rest.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun feared Zhou Yi so deeply that his face burned even in winter and he fanned himself without cease.

sentences.zh: 敦使繆坦籍顗家，收得素簏數枚，盛故絮而已，酒五甕，米數石，在位者服其清約。

translations.literal: Dun sent Miu Tan to inventory Yi's house; they obtained several plain baskets, holding old wadding only; five jars of wine, several dan of rice—those in office admired his purity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's men searched his home and found only old padding in baskets, a few jars of wine, and a little rice—officials marveled at his austerity.

sentences.zh: 敦卒後，追贈左光祿大夫、儀同三司，諡曰康，祀以少牢。

translations.literal: After Dun died, posthumously gifted left household grandee, peerage equal to Three Offices, posthumous title Kang, sacrificed with lesser beast offering.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun's death Zhou Yi was canonized as left household grandee with Three Dukes parity, posthumous name "Kang," and a lesser beast sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 初，敦之舉兵也，劉隗勸帝盡除諸王，司空導率群從詣闕請罪，值顗將入，導呼顗謂曰：「伯仁，以百口累卿！

translations.literal: At first, when Dun raised troops, Liu Kui urged the emperor to exterminate all the princes; minister of works Dao led host of followers to the palace gate to confess guilt; it happened Yi was about to enter; Dao called Yi and said: "Boren, I entrust my hundred mouths to you!
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled, Liu Kui urged executing the Sima princes; Wang Dao led his clan to beg mercy at the gate; seeing Zhou Yi arrive, he cried, "Boren, my family's hundred lives rest with you!

sentences.zh: 」顗直入不顧。

translations.literal: " Yi went straight in without looking back.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Yi walked past without a word.

sentences.zh: 既見帝，言導忠誠，申救甚至，帝納其言。

translations.literal: Having seen the emperor, he spoke Dao's loyalty and sincerity, pleaded rescue to the utmost; the emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Before the throne he pleaded Wang Dao's loyalty until the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 顗喜飲酒，致醉而出。

translations.literal: Yi loved drinking wine, to the point of drunk then went out.
translations.idiomatic: He celebrated with wine and left drunk.

sentences.zh: 導猶在門，又呼顗。

translations.literal: Dao was still at the gate, again called Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao still waited at the gate and called after him.

sentences.zh: 顗不與言，顧左右曰：「今年殺諸賊奴，取金印如斗大繫肘。

translations.literal: Yi did not speak with him, looked to left and right saying: "This year we will kill the various bandit slaves, take gold seals as big as a dou and tie them on the elbow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi ignored him and muttered to attendants about killing "bandit slaves" and winning great seals—drunk boasting.

sentences.zh: 」既出，又上表明導，言甚切至。

translations.literal: Having gone out, again submitted memorial clarifying Dao, words extremely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Sober, he filed a sober memorial strongly defending Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 導不知救己，而甚銜之。

translations.literal: Dao did not know he had rescued himself, yet deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao never knew Zhou Yi had saved him and nursed a bitter grudge.

sentences.zh: 敦既得志，問導曰：「周顗、戴若思南北之望，當登三司，無所疑也。

translations.literal: When Dun had obtained his will, he asked Dao: "Zhou Yi and Dai Ruosi are south and north's expectations; they ought to ascend Three Offices—without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: After his victory Wang Dun asked Wang Dao whether Zhou Yi and Dai Ruosi should be given the Three Dukes' rank.

sentences.zh: 」導不答。

translations.literal: " Dao did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「若不三司，便應令僕邪？

translations.literal: Again said: "If not Three Offices, then ought to order vice director?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun pressed, "If not the Three Dukes, then vice director?

sentences.zh: 」又不答。

translations.literal: " Again did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Again no answer.

sentences.zh: 敦曰：「若不爾，正當誅爾。

translations.literal: Dun said: "If not thus, then ought to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: "Then I must kill them," Wang Dun said.

sentences.zh: 」導又無言。

translations.literal: " Dao again had no words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao still said nothing—consent by silence.

sentences.zh: 導後料檢中書故事，見顗表救己，殷勤款至。

translations.literal: Dao afterward examined central document archives, saw Yi's memorial rescuing himself, earnest and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Dao found Zhou Yi's memorial in the archives and saw how fervently he had pleaded for him.

sentences.zh: 導執表流涕，悲不自勝，告其諸子曰：「吾雖不殺伯仁，伯仁由我而死。

translations.literal: Dao grasped the memorial and shed tears, grief not self-controlled, told his various sons: "Although I did not kill Boren, Boren died because of me.
translations.idiomatic: He wept and told his sons, "I did not strike the blow, yet Boren died through me.

sentences.zh: 幽冥之中，負此良友！

translations.literal: In the dark world, I have failed this good friend!
translations.idiomatic: In the world below I owe him that debt.

sentences.zh: 」顗三子：閔、恬、頤。

translations.literal: " Yi had three sons: Min, Tian, Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi left three sons: Zhou Min, Zhou Tian, and Zhou Yi (junior).

sentences.zh: 閔字子騫，方直有父風。

translations.literal: Min's courtesy name was Ziqian, square and straight, had father's air.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Min, courtesy name Ziqian, was as blunt and upright as his father.

sentences.zh: 曆衡陽、建安、臨川太守，侍中，中領軍，吏部尚書，尚書左僕射，加中軍將軍，轉護軍，領秘書監。

translations.literal: He passed through Hengyang, Jian'an, Linchuan administrators, attendant-in-ordinary, central army commander, minister of personnel, left vice director of the secretariat, added central army general, transferred guards commander, concurrently palace librarian supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He governed several commanderies, served as palace attendant, central commander, minister of personnel, left vice director, central army general, general of the guards, and palace librarian.

sentences.zh: 卒，追贈金紫光祿大夫，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: He died, posthumously gifted golden purple household grandee, posthumous title Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was canonized golden purple grandee with posthumous name "Lie" (Ardent).

sentences.zh: 無子，以弟頤長子琳為嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, he took younger brother Yi's eldest son Lin as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he adopted his brother's son Zhou Lin.

sentences.zh: 琳仕至東陽太守。

translations.literal: Lin's office reached Dongyang administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lin rose to governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 恬、頤並曆卿守。

translations.literal: Tian and Yi both passed through minister and governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tian and the younger Zhou Yi both held ministerial and provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 琳少子文，驃騎諮議參軍

translations.literal: Lin's youngest son Wen, swift cavalry deliberation military adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lin's youngest son Zhou Wen served as deliberation adviser on the swift cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫太剛則折，至察無徒，以之為政，則害于而國；

translations.literal: The historian says: Too rigid and one snaps; too scrutinizing and one has no followers—to use this in governing harms your state;
translations.idiomatic: The chroniclers say: excess rigidity snaps; hyper-criticism wins no allies—rule that way and the state suffers;

sentences.zh: 用之行己，則凶於乃家。

translations.literal: to use it in conducting oneself brings misfortune to your house.
translations.idiomatic: live that way and your house comes to grief.

sentences.zh: 誠以器乖容眾，非先王之道也。

translations.literal: Truly because the vessel rejects holding the multitude—it is not the way of former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Such temperaments cannot embrace the many; they are not the way of the ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 大連司憲，陰候主情，當約法之秋，獻斫棺之議。

translations.literal: Dalian presided over the laws, secretly watched the ruler's mood; in the season of tightening statutes, offered the proposal to hew the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui enforced the code while reading the emperor's every mood; in a time of harsh justice he urged even posthumous punishment.

sentences.zh: 玄亮剛愎，與物多違，雖有崇上之心，專行刻下之化，同薄相濟，並運天機。

translations.literal: Xuanliang was stubborn and self-willed, with things often at odds; although he had mind to exalt superiors, he exclusively practiced carving-down transformation; same meanness mutually aided, together they moved heaven's mechanism.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie was willful and abrasive; though he meant to strengthen the throne, he ground men down—petty minds in league, they shifted the court's fate.

sentences.zh: 是使賢宰見疏，致物情於解體；

translations.literal: This made worthy shepherds seen as distant, led the world's temper to come apart;
translations.idiomatic: Good ministers were driven off and the realm's heart broke;

sentences.zh: 權臣發怒，借其名以誓師。

translations.literal: the powerful minister grew angry, borrowed their names to swear the host.
translations.idiomatic: a warlord seized on their names to muster his hosts.

sentences.zh: 既而謀人之國，國危而苟免；

translations.literal: Thereupon plotting against others' state, the state endangered yet they barely escaped;
translations.idiomatic: They plotted for the realm yet, when danger came, saved themselves;

sentences.zh: 見昵於主，主辱而圖生。

translations.literal: favored by the ruler, yet when the ruler suffered shame they schemed to live.
translations.idiomatic: trusted by the throne, they fled when the throne was shamed.

sentences.zh: 自取流亡，非不幸也。

translations.literal: They brought exile on themselves—it was not misfortune without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Their banishment was no accident.

sentences.zh: 若思閑爽，照理研幽。

translations.literal: Ruosi was open and bright, illumined pattern and probed the subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Ruosi was magnanimous and acute, a subtle reasoner.

sentences.zh: 伯仁凝正，處腴能約。

translations.literal: Boren was grave and upright, in plenty able to be frugal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi was stern and honest, austere even amid plenty.

sentences.zh: 咸以高才雅道，參豫疇咨。

translations.literal: All by lofty talent and elegant way participated in counsel and consultation.
translations.idiomatic: All three brought high gifts and refinement to the council chamber.

sentences.zh: 及京室淪胥，抗言無撓，甘赴鼎而全操，蓋事君而盡節者歟！

translations.literal: When the capital house sank, they spoke straight without bending, willingly went to the cauldron yet preserved integrity—are they not those who served the ruler and exhausted steadfastness!
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell they spoke without flinching and went to death with honor—true servants of the throne.

sentences.zh: 顗招時論，尤其酒德，《禮經》曰「瑕不掩瑜」，未足韜其美也。

translations.literal: Yi invited contemporary discussion, especially in wine virtue; the "Book of Rites" says "flaws do not mask jade's luster"—not enough to hide his beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi drew gossip for his drinking, yet as the Rites say, a flaw does not hide the jade—his virtues still shine.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：劉刁亮直，志奉興王。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Liu and Diao were bright and straight, mind served the rising king.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict reads: Liu Kui and Diao Xie were blunt loyalists who served the restoration.

sentences.zh: 奸回醜正，終致奔亡。

translations.literal: Villainy warped the upright, in the end brought flight and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Vice turned virtue upside down and ended in exile.

sentences.zh: 周戴英爽，忠謨允塞。

translations.literal: Zhou and Dai were heroic and bright, loyal plans truly filled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi and Dai Ruosi were gallant and true, their counsel full of integrity.

sentences.zh: 道屬屯蒙，禍罹凶慝。

translations.literal: The Way met hardship and darkness; calamity fell from vicious evil.
translations.idiomatic: The age was dark and cruel fortune struck them down.
